issues.body:
## Overview

What is this document? This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” cool-down, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope for this document? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

## Previous version notes

* Released Aug 4, 2026: included 11 Evalchemy benchmarks, 14 lm-eval-harness tasks, 7 Harbor agentic evals and 5 AA-II component benchmarks named as weighting targets but not run directly

## Complete eval list, with hyperparameters

### In Distribution

| Eval | Framework | Metric | Shots | Repetitions | Allowed context length | Mean time-to-complete |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| MATH500 | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 7m 55s |
| AIME24 | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 10 runs × 10 samples per item; base seeds 42–51 | 73,664 tokens | 12m 16s |
| HumanEvalPlus | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 58s |
| MBPPPlus | Evalchemy | accuracy | 3 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 3m 44s |
| OlympiadBench (30-question subset) | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 10 samples per item; base seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 1h 27m |
| MMLU-Pro | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 65,536 tokens | — |
| GPQA Diamond | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 3 samples per item; base seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 28m 44s |
| CruxEval | Evalchemy | accuracy (input and output prediction, reported separately) | 1 | 1 run × 1 sample per item and direction; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 36m 31s |
| FinanceBench | Evalchemy | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 9m 23s |
| IFBench | Evalchemy | accuracy (strict, prompt-level) | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 2m 18s |
| MRCR | Evalchemy | mean sequence similarity | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 37m 35s |
| `gsm8k` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 5m 10s |
| `mmlu` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 5 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 37m 36s |
| `piqa` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 2m 03s |
| `winogrande` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 5 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 1m 48s |
| `openbookqa` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 1m 19s |
| `boolq` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 3m 41s |
| `truthfulqa_mc2` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 3m 28s |
| `triviaqa` | lm-eval-harness | accuracy | 5 | 1 run × 1 sample per item; seed 42 | 73,664 tokens | 31m 24s |
| SWE-bench Verified random-100 | Harbor | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 agent trial per item | 32,768 input tokens | — |
| OT-TBLite | Harbor | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 agent trial per item | 32,768 input tokens | — |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 | Harbor | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 agent trial per item | 32,768 input tokens | — |
| SimpleQA mini-200 | Harbor | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 agent trial per item | 32,768 input tokens | — |
| DS-1000 mini-200 | Harbor | accuracy | 0 | 1 run × 1 agent trial per item | 32,768 input tokens | — |

Evalchemy ran against a server configured for 73,728 tokens. Marin reserves a 64-token transport
margin, yielding the 73,664-token evaluator allowance shown above; MMLU-Pro has a stricter
65,536-token benchmark cap. Harbor's Terminus-2 policy independently limits model input to 32,768
tokens and model output to 8,192 tokens.

`SimpleQA mini-200` and `DS-1000 mini-200` are fixed seed-42 random samples of their full
registry datasets. Harbor records the selected task names and immutable source revisions in
`simpleqa@mini-200` and `ds-1000@mini-200`; every model must use the same 200 tasks.

### Out of Distribution

* AAII 4.3

### How do we handle in-distribution and out-of-distribution evals?

#### IN-DISTRIBUTION

**We will** -- dedup against our SFT data, look at model scores while we develop the model, inspect the correlation of our ID evals with our OOD evals

**We may** -- develop synthetic RL tasks modeled on specific tasks in ID evals

**We will not** -- train on teacher rollouts from eval questions, use our ID eval instructions directly as the basis of RL data

#### OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION

**We will** -- de-dup against our SFT raw data, look at meta-data about these evals (e.g., how big they are, general knowledge domain, etc), eval baselines on these evals

**We will not** -- look at the individual questions in the evals, look at any of our own model scores from these evals until our model is frozen, model any synthetic tasks on tasks in the evals (edited)

### Metric definitions

- **Accuracy:** the number of scored examples whose configured grader or verifier returns a correct outcome, divided by the number of scored examples. This includes exact-match rate, pass@1 with one completion, and agent-task solve rate with one trial. FinanceBench and SimpleQA mini-200 use an LLM judge; SimpleQA counts only `CORRECT` as correct, while `INCORRECT` and `NOT_ATTEMPTED` both score zero. For `piqa` and `openbookqa`, the selected answer is the option with the highest length-normalized log-likelihood (`acc_norm` in lm-eval-harness), and accuracy is the fraction of those selections that are correct. AIME24 reports the mean accuracy across its ten seeded runs.
- **CruxEval accuracy:** reported separately for input prediction and output prediction. Input prediction asks the model to reconstruct a valid function input from the code and desired output; output prediction asks it to predict the output from the code and input.
- **IFBench strict prompt-level accuracy:** the fraction of prompts for which the raw response satisfies every required constraint.
- **Mean sequence similarity:** MRCR's mean `SequenceMatcher` ratio between the response's answer span and the reference answer. A response that fails MRCR's nonce check receives zero credit.
- **Allowed context length:** This is allowed prompt + completion context length. If a model's maximum context length is less than the allowed context length, we adopt the model's maximum context length. For single-turn benchmarks, we subdivide the space into max prompt length = longest prompt in the dataset plus a bit of cushion, max response length = the remaining context window. For multi-turn benchmarks, max generation length per turn is 8192.

### Valid (Scoreable) Harbor Exceptions

For a single-step Harbor task, the following agent-terminal exceptions are valid,
scoreable outcomes when the trial also contains a completed `verifier_result`:

- `AgentTimeoutError`: the agent reached its configured execution timeout; Harbor preserves
  the work produced so far and runs the verifier.
- `ContextLengthExceededError`: the model or agent exhausted the available context; Harbor
  treats that as a classified end to the attempt and runs the verifier.
- `TurnCapExhaustedError`: the agent reached its configured turn cap without declaring
  completion; Harbor runs the verifier on the resulting state.
- `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError`: the agent process exited non-zero after potentially producing
  scoreable work; Harbor still runs the verifier. Agent-specific subclasses must be reported
  under their concrete exception type and reviewed for validity rather than silently grouped.

An exception is not sufficient evidence that a trial was scored. Include a trial in the
scoreable denominator only when `verifier_result` is present. Environment, setup, whole-trial,
artifact-collection, and verifier failures—including `AgentSetupTimeoutError`,
`EnvironmentStartTimeoutError`, `TrialTimeoutError`, `VerifierTimeoutError`,
`TrialNotScoredError`, and `VerificationNotCompletedError`—are unscored infrastructure or
harness outcomes and must be retried or reported separately. Likewise, errors such as model
authentication failures or agents killed by infrastructure are not valid model outcomes merely
because their Python classes inherit from `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError`.

## Codebase pins

| Codebase | `main` commit |
| --- | --- |
| Harbor | [`7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a) |
| Evalchemy | [`65c80022b8be98012a4ce6cd98a5168a7a58d99e`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/65c80022b8be98012a4ce6cd98a5168a7a58d99e) |
| Marin | [`a5773eb75bda715f160cbd34e2552092cc2935e9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/a5773eb75bda715f160cbd34e2552092cc2935e9) |

## Eval launch commands (Marin)

These commands require an Iris account with access to the `marin` controller and the `cw-rno2a`
federated cluster. `MODEL_CONFIG` must be an absolute path to a Marin model-catalog YAML file whose
model and tokenizer revisions are immutable. The model must support a 73,728-token context for MRCR.
The checkout below is the public campaign revision based on the pinned Marin `main` commit above. It
adds the Evalchemy revision that correctly applies the zero-shot MMLU-Pro policy.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/marin-community/marin.git
cd marin
git checkout ba2fef7443dd5fad1b1a35402982e1c4ce71c8c0
uv sync --all-packages

export MODEL_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/pinned-model.yaml
export TOGETHER_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_API_KEY="$TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_BASE_URL=https://api.together.xyz/v1
export JUDGE_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-120b

POLICY_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)

write_chat_config() {
  config_name=$1
  task_name=$2
  runtime_extra=$3
  max_tokens=$4
  max_length=$5
  {
    echo "tasks: [$task_name]"
    echo "task_options:"
    echo "  $task_name:"
    echo "    num_fewshot: 0"
    echo "    task_alias: $config_name"
    echo "    generation: true"
    echo "apply_chat_template: true"
    echo "batch_size: 1"
    echo "seed: 42"
    echo "max_tokens: $max_tokens"
    if [ "$max_length" != "default" ]; then
      echo "max_length: $max_length"
    fi
    echo "runtime_extras: [$runtime_extra]"
  } > "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/$config_name.yaml"
}

write_chat_config mmlu-pro MMLUPro mmlupro 32768 65536
write_chat_config gpqa-diamond GPQADiamond gpqadiamond 32768 default
write_chat_config cruxeval CruxEval cruxeval 2048 default
write_chat_config financebench FinanceBench financebench 4096 default
write_chat_config ifbench IFBench ifbench 1024 default
write_chat_config mrcr MRCR mrcr 4096 73728

# Deterministic single-run Evalchemy and lm-eval-harness evaluations.
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
  --evals math500,humanevalplus,mbppplus,olympiadbench,gsm8k-0shot,mmlu,piqa,winogrande,openbookqa,boolq,truthfulqa,triviaqa \
  --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
  --priority interactive \
  --version eval-policy-updated

# AIME24: ten independent launches; Evalchemy generates ten responses per question in each launch.
for seed in $(seq 42 51); do
  uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
    --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
    --evals aime24 \
    --seed "$seed" \
    --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
    --priority interactive \
    --version eval-policy-updated
done

# Policy additions that are not registered as named Marin eval keys at the pinned Marin commit.
uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/mmlu-pro.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/gpqa-diamond.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/cruxeval.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/financebench.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/ifbench.yaml" \
  --evalchemy-config "$POLICY_CONFIG_DIR/mrcr.yaml" \
  --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
  --priority interactive \
  --version eval-policy-updated

# The campaign's five Harbor policies are pinned on its public experiment branch.
for config_name in swebench-recovery ot-tblite-recovery tb2-recovery simpleqa-recovery ds-1000-local; do
  curl -fsSL \
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/8aa9a354d30abbda89a7756e11c1a37037aa8a65/experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/$config_name.yaml" \
    -o "experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/$config_name.yaml"
done

# Select the policy's deterministic seed-42 mini datasets from the pinned Harbor registry.
export HARBOR_REGISTRY_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/harbor/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a/registry.json
uv run python - "$HARBOR_REGISTRY_URL" <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

registry_url = sys.argv[1]
config_dir = Path("experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor")
for filename, dataset_name in (
    ("simpleqa-recovery.yaml", "simpleqa"),
    ("ds-1000-local.yaml", "ds-1000"),
):
    path = config_dir / filename
    policy = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
    policy["datasets"] = [
        {
            "name": dataset_name,
            "version": "mini-200",
            "registry_url": registry_url,
        }
    ]
    if dataset_name == "ds-1000":
        # DS-1000's registry tasks must build their pinned Dockerfiles; no
        # published prebuilt image is available for this dataset version.
        policy.setdefault("environment", {})["force_build"] = True
    path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(policy, sort_keys=False))
PY

uv run python -m experiments.evaluation.cli launch \
  --model-config "$MODEL_CONFIG" \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/swebench-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/ot-tblite-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/tb2-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/simpleqa-recovery.yaml \
  --harbor-config experiments/evaluation/configs/harbor/ds-1000-local.yaml \
  --federated_cluster cw-rno2a \
  --priority interactive \
  --version eval-policy-updated
```

## Eval launch commands (Standalone)

The standalone path requires an OpenAI-compatible endpoint reachable from both the local evaluator
and Daytona sandboxes. `MODEL_BASE_URL` is the API root ending in `/v1`; `MODEL_ID` must match the
model name returned by its `/models` endpoint; and `TOKENIZER_ID` must be an immutable Hugging Face
model or tokenizer revision. Evalchemy executes generated code for HumanEvalPlus and MBPPPlus.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy.git
cd evalchemy
git checkout 65c80022b8be98012a4ce6cd98a5168a7a58d99e
uv sync --python 3.12 --extra benchmarks --extra serve-eval

export MODEL_BASE_URL=https://example-model-endpoint.invalid/v1
export MODEL_ID="REPLACE_WITH_SERVED_MODEL_NAME"
export MODEL_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_MODEL_ENDPOINT_API_KEY"
export TOKENIZER_ID="REPLACE_WITH_HUGGING_FACE_TOKENIZER_ID"
export TOKENIZER_REVISION="REPLACE_WITH_IMMUTABLE_TOKENIZER_REVISION"
export TOGETHER_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_API_KEY="$TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export JUDGE_BASE_URL=https://api.together.xyz/v1
export JUDGE_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-120b

mkdir -p results/evalchemy

run_chat_eval() {
  task_name=$1
  num_fewshot=$2
  max_tokens=$3
  max_length=$4
  seed=$5
  output_name=$6
  shift 6
  uv run eval \
    --model local-chat-completions \
    --model_args "model=$MODEL_ID,base_url=${MODEL_BASE_URL%/}/chat/completions,api_key=$MODEL_API_KEY,tokenizer=$TOKENIZER_ID,revision=$TOKENIZER_REVISION,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=8,timeout=1800,max_length=$max_length" \
    --tasks "$task_name" \
    --num_fewshot "$num_fewshot" \
    --batch_size 1 \
    --seed "$seed" \
    --max_length "$max_length" \
    --max_tokens "$max_tokens" \
    --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=$max_tokens" \
    --apply_chat_template \
    --log_samples \
    --output_path "results/evalchemy/$output_name" \
    "$@"
}

run_completion_eval() {
  task_name=$1
  num_fewshot=$2
  max_tokens=$3
  max_length=$4
  uv run eval \
    --model local-completions \
    --model_args "model=$MODEL_ID,base_url=${MODEL_BASE_URL%/}/completions,api_key=$MODEL_API_KEY,tokenizer=$TOKENIZER_ID,revision=$TOKENIZER_REVISION,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=8,timeout=1800,max_length=$max_length" \
    --tasks "$task_name" \
    --num_fewshot "$num_fewshot" \
    --batch_size 1 \
    --seed 42 \
    --max_length "$max_length" \
    --max_tokens "$max_tokens" \
    --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=$max_tokens" \
    --log_samples \
    --output_path "results/evalchemy/$task_name"
}

run_chat_eval MATH500 0 8192 73664 42 math500
for seed in $(seq 42 51); do
  run_chat_eval AIME24 0 8192 73664 "$seed" "aime24-seed-$seed"
done
run_chat_eval HumanEvalPlus 0 1024 73664 42 humanevalplus --confirm_run_unsafe_code
run_chat_eval MBPPPlus 0 1024 73664 42 mbppplus --confirm_run_unsafe_code
run_chat_eval OlympiadBench 0 32768 73664 42 olympiadbench
run_chat_eval MMLUPro 0 32768 65536 42 mmlu-pro
run_chat_eval GPQADiamond 0 32768 73664 42 gpqa-diamond
run_chat_eval CruxEval 0 2048 73664 42 cruxeval
run_chat_eval FinanceBench 0 4096 73664 42 financebench
run_chat_eval IFBench 0 1024 73664 42 ifbench
run_chat_eval MRCR 0 4096 73664 42 mrcr

run_completion_eval gsm8k 0 512 73664
run_completion_eval mmlu 5 256 73664
run_completion_eval piqa 0 256 73664
run_completion_eval winogrande 5 256 73664
run_completion_eval openbookqa 0 256 73664
run_completion_eval boolq 0 256 73664
run_completion_eval truthfulqa_mc2 0 256 73664
run_completion_eval triviaqa 5 128 73664
```

Run the Harbor evaluations from a separate directory so Harbor's environment does not share
Evalchemy's project environment:

```bash
cd ..
uv tool install --force \
  "harbor @ git+https://github.com/marin-community/harbor.git@7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a"

export MODEL_BASE_URL=https://example-model-endpoint.invalid/v1
export MODEL_ID="REPLACE_WITH_SERVED_MODEL_NAME"
export MODEL_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_MODEL_ENDPOINT_API_KEY"
export TOGETHER_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_TOGETHER_API_KEY"
export DAYTONA_API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_DAYTONA_API_KEY"

HARBOR_AGENTIC_CONFIG=$(mktemp)
cat > "$HARBOR_AGENTIC_CONFIG" <<'YAML'
n_concurrent_trials: 16
release_trial_payloads_in_memory: true
retry:
  max_retries: 10
  include_exceptions:
    - InternalServerError
    - APIConnectionError
    - APITimeoutError
    - ArtifactUploadTimeoutError
    - ArtifactWriterBacklogError
    - CancelledError
    - ContextManagementInfrastructureError
    - LLMRequestTimeoutError
    - SandboxBuildFailedError
    - TrialTimeoutError
  wait_multiplier: 2.0
  min_wait_sec: 1.0
  max_wait_sec: 60.0
environment:
  type: daytona
agents:
  - name: terminus-2
    kwargs:
      model_info:
        max_input_tokens: 32768
        max_output_tokens: 8192
        input_cost_per_token: 0.0
        output_cost_per_token: 0.0
datasets:
  - name: hf://DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders
    ref: 0c553bd6d05d451907afb8db31dba84759ccc993
  - name: openthoughts-tblite
    version: "2.0"
    registry_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/harbor/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a/registry.json
  - name: hf://DCAgent2/terminal_bench_2
    ref: 693231ec029249e7c91ed2e414bcc9c45d7cd879
  - name: simpleqa
    version: mini-200
    registry_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/harbor/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a/registry.json
verifier:
  env:
    OPENAI_API_KEY: "${TOGETHER_API_KEY}"
    OPENAI_BASE_URL: https://api.together.xyz/v1
    MODEL_NAME: openai/gpt-oss-120b
YAML

harbor run \
  --config "$HARBOR_AGENTIC_CONFIG" \
  --model "hosted_vllm/$MODEL_ID" \
  --ak "api_base=${MODEL_BASE_URL%/}" \
  --ae "OPENAI_API_KEY=$MODEL_API_KEY" \
  --jobs-dir results/harbor/agentic \
  --yes

# DS-1000 uses its own config because its task Dockerfiles must be built from
# source. Applying force_build to the other datasets would change their runtime.
DS1000_CONFIG=$(mktemp)
cat > "$DS1000_CONFIG" <<'YAML'
n_concurrent_trials: 16
release_trial_payloads_in_memory: true
retry:
  max_retries: 10
  include_exceptions:
    - InternalServerError
    - APIConnectionError
    - APITimeoutError
    - ArtifactUploadTimeoutError
    - ArtifactWriterBacklogError
    - CancelledError
    - ContextManagementInfrastructureError
    - LLMRequestTimeoutError
    - SandboxBuildFailedError
    - TrialTimeoutError
  wait_multiplier: 2.0
  min_wait_sec: 1.0
  max_wait_sec: 60.0
environment:
  type: daytona
  force_build: true
agents:
  - name: terminus-2
    kwargs:
      model_info:
        max_input_tokens: 32768
        max_output_tokens: 8192
        input_cost_per_token: 0.0
        output_cost_per_token: 0.0
datasets:
  - name: ds-1000
    version: mini-200
    registry_url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/harbor/7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a/registry.json
YAML

harbor run \
  --config "$DS1000_CONFIG" \
  --model "hosted_vllm/$MODEL_ID" \
  --ak "api_base=${MODEL_BASE_URL%/}" \
  --ae "OPENAI_API_KEY=$MODEL_API_KEY" \
  --jobs-dir results/harbor/ds-1000-mini-200 \
  --yes
```

## Standards for presenting Marin evals

* For each benchmark, plot Snowball perf, along with baseline(s) perf, on an x-y scatterplot, with y being perf and x being total training FLOPS
* Use 6ND proxy for pretraining and SFT FLOPS, and 6 * max_tokens_per_rollout / max_context_length * n_rollouts * active_params proxy for RL FLOPS
* In a separate standalone table, include all raw scores in XX.y format, with 95% confidence intervals derived from the trial count -- do not leave gaps, use table captions for results that require further context, use the exact same model family in the table as was present in the x-y scatterplot(s)
* Eval results are reportable IFF the eval in question completed with <10% of trials encountering infrastructure errors
* Eval results are reportable IFF they include provenance, in the form of model traces, and where available, verifier traces
* Any eval result that is publicly presented should clearly distinguish whether the benchmarks are in-distribution (part of the dev set), held out, or a mix of the two
* Any eval result that is publicly presented in a major release should report on *all* ID and OOD benchmarks, avoiding cherry picking, substitution, or new evals outside of a formal policy update
* For active development and internal communication, it is fine to define working subsets of the ID benchmarks and report on those in isolation

## Future considerations

* We would like to post-train multiple Snowball checkpoints, experimenting with different degrees of compute applied to post-training, to establish trade-off lines / domains
* We would like to think about a "marin model card" that would set minimum standards for true open development

👍 

I'm on board with the set of evaluations and how to run them, and I like that we'll have a policy for what we can look at. My proposal re pins:

* We define this as Marin Eval Policy v0.1
* Pins indicate the behavior now
* If we need to move the pins (to update to a new version of Iris, etc)
  - We rerun the eval suites with a representative model(s) - Qwen + Snowball
  - If the suites are identical (within noise), we update pins in place
  - If not, we need to bump the version
* Results should be reported at a particular version
* Updating the version should be infrequent but acceptable: a totally broken eval for example

I think the bulk of the value here is being transparent about all of the appropriate parameters and command lines for running we're using for the evaluations, and that we'll do our best to keep these aligned. I want us to balance the desire for replication with flexibility for making code changes, so hopefully the above tradeoff seems fair.

issues.title: Marin Eval Policy (2026-09-16)

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Marin cannot run FinanceBench or SimpleQA with a Together-backed judge without replacing or exposing candidate-endpoint credentials. A direct Together probe confirmed that `openai/gpt-oss-120b` supports the Chat Completions API used by FinanceBench and the Responses API request shape used by SimpleQA, so provider compatibility is not the blocker.

Reproduce:
1. Launch FinanceBench with a distinct external judge credential. [`runner.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/93251781092fa281077dff0a9c7b455fd6cc9677/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L229-L235) overwrites `OPENAI_API_KEY` with `local-endpoint` in the Evalchemy child.
2. Launch a supplied Harbor SimpleQA policy whose verifier requires a separate provider key. [`HarborDefinition.secret_env_for`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/93251781092fa281077dff0a9c7b455fd6cc9677/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L117-L120) resolves only the Daytona credential, so the isolated verifier does not receive the judge key.
3. Observe that FinanceBench cannot authenticate to the judge and SimpleQA has no verifier credential. Passing the Together key as the process-wide `OPENAI_API_KEY` would also send a judge credential through the candidate client boundary.

Expected: Evalchemy judges and Harbor verifiers receive explicit provider key, base URL, and model settings at verifier-only boundaries. Candidate endpoint authentication remains unchanged. Judge transport and parsing failures fail evaluation coverage instead of becoming incorrect answers.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

Current main already resolves Harbor verifier placeholders through [`HarborDefinition.secret_env_for`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b15614b09f7a976a8e075d2b36233b59991cb7e/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L124-L128), so that part of the report is fixed. Evalchemy still has no judge configuration and its child reserves `OPENAI_API_KEY` for candidate authentication in [`runner.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5b15614b09f7a976a8e075d2b36233b59991cb7e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L226-L236). The pinned FinanceBench and SimpleQA graders accept ambiguous output as a grade; SimpleQA also needs a new immutable generated-dataset revision. PR [#9128](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9128) owns hosted judge provisioning and does not provide the external credential path.

**Proposed Fix**

Add a FinanceBench-only typed judge block that maps a `SecretSpec` to `JUDGE_API_KEY`, passes its URL and model separately, and records only those non-secret fields. Tighten both grader parsers so malformed labels and provider failures reduce coverage instead of producing zero rewards. Regenerate and pin the corrected SimpleQA dataset, then validate isolation with separate local candidate and judge HTTP stubs.

issues.title: [evals] External judges cannot receive provider credentials safely

issues.author: gonzalobenegas
issues.body:
Status: the first pilot has 32 synthetic tasks and 31 accepted teacher trajectories. The SFT comparison is pending. See the [pilot record and artifact locations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9257#issuecomment-5781700724).

Generate synthetic training data for computational biology, starting with task families covered by designated in-distribution (ID) biology evaluations. Produce executable Harbor tasks and teacher trajectories with per-attempt rewards for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), with validated tasks also available for later reinforcement learning (RL).

The initial question is whether we can generate biologically meaningful, solvable tasks with reliable graders at a useful cost. Effects on model performance would require a subsequent training experiment.

Scope:

- Generate new tasks that exercise skills represented in the selected ID evaluations, with fresh inputs and independently established expected results. Candidate sources include biological datasets, analysis workflows, and bioinformatics repositories.
- Follow [Marin's evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): exclude out-of-distribution evaluations from task design, deduplicate against evaluation data, and keep teacher rollouts on evaluation questions out of training. ID evaluation instructions must not be used directly as RL data.
- Keep the implementation in `marin-community/marin` on an experimental branch, provisionally under `experiments/post_training/bio_tasks/`. A merge to `main` is not a prerequisite for this experiment. Record the code revision and any local changes used for each run.

Candidate approaches:

1. Generate tasks from a description of an ID task family, specifying new data, an analysis objective, expected outputs, and a verifier. For example, construct a differential-expression analysis task over a different dataset and compute reference outputs independently.
2. Derive tasks from biological code or workflows through instruction backtranslation, or adapt a repository-based generation recipe such as [SWE-smith](https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-smith) or [SERA](https://github.com/allenai/SERA). Packaging these tasks for Harbor and establishing a trustworthy grader are separate steps.

Start with one approach and one task family. GLM-5.3 is a candidate teacher; record the model identity and generation settings actually used. Reuse Marin's existing launch and rollout machinery where applicable, and preserve Marin's evaluation defaults for benchmark comparisons.

Existing work to reuse:

- [Scientific-repository backtranslation (#7813)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7813): related Marin work covering bioinformatics repositories. The issue names uncommitted implementation files that were absent from `main` when inspected; locate the working branch before planning to reuse them.
- [OpenThoughts-Agent self-instruct](https://github.com/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-Agent/tree/main/data/self_instruct): task generation from source text, with separate verifier-authoring code. Adapt useful components after inspecting their behavior and dependencies, preserving applicable licenses and attribution.
- [Marin's TaskTrove pipeline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/main/experiments/post_training/tasktrove): an existing pattern for converting, validating, deduplicating, and recording the provenance of Harbor tasks.

Pilot work:

- [ ] Select the ID task family and source material; document what the generated tasks should test.
- [ ] Generate Harbor tasks containing instructions, input data, an environment, a reference solution, and a verifier. Keep reference answers unavailable to the solving agent.
- [ ] Review a sample for biological validity and instruction clarity. Check that reference solutions pass and deliberately incorrect or empty outputs fail; record rejected tasks and reasons.
- [ ] Check for overlap with evaluation data and duplicates within the generated set. Retain source identifiers and generation provenance.
- [ ] Collect teacher attempts on accepted synthetic tasks. Retain traces, rewards, model failures, and infrastructure failures before applying any SFT selection rule.
- [ ] Report accepted and rejected task counts, verifier defects, teacher success rates, token usage, runtime, and estimated cost. Record limitations and negative results alongside the artifacts.

The pilot is complete when its task dataset and reward-bearing trajectories can be inspected and reproduced, with a documented decision to expand, revise, or stop the recipe. A useful negative result also completes the pilot. Any claim of improved biology capability requires a training comparison under a fixed evaluation protocol.

issues.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball. This includes selecting benchmarks, defining comparable protocols, supporting their execution in Marin, and following results across models and checkpoints. The initial evaluation paths are non-agentic questions through Evalchemy and agentic biological analysis through Harbor.

Use Marin's existing protocols where available. Report question-answering and agentic-task results separately, with explicit task coverage and aggregation rules. Keep evaluation items isolated from training data.

Current GLM-5.3 baselines (updated September 22, 2026):

| Benchmark / protocol | Correct / graded | Graded / attempted | Reported score | Agent solving time / question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MMLU biology, Evalchemy | 462 / 554 | 554 / 554 (100%) | 81.79% mean of subject accuracies; 83.39% pooled accuracy | Not applicable (non-agentic) |
| [BixBench CLI v1.5, Harbor](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) | 101 / 187 | 187 / 205 (91.22%) | 54.01% among graded questions | Median **5.6 min**; middle 50% **1.7–15.5 min**; p90 **37.3 min**. 17/205 reached the 60-min cap. Excludes setup/grading. [Breakdown](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744679901) |
| [BixBench-Verified-50 v1.0 / decimal-precision-v1](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) | 42 / 49 | 49 / 50 (98%) | 85.71% among graded questions; saved-answer regrade | Median **2.6 min**; p90 **15.7 min**; max **55.3 min**. Excludes setup/grading. [Breakdown](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766814742) |

The BixBench run attempted all 205 questions and retains 18 ungraded outcomes: fourteen missing answers after the one-hour agent limit, two killed sandbox processes, one gateway failure, and one judge error. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is 43.79–63.43%. Ten of eleven failed grading calls were recovered using saved answers; all 177 valid native grades and original artifacts were preserved, with no solver reruns.

BixBench uses Terminus-2 and Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, with the [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800), the unchanged binary-equivalence prompt, and disclosed 10 GiB disk / AMD64 image overrides. This is an exploratory CLI baseline. The replacement judge, answer-precision sensitivity, reference inconsistencies, missing grades, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons. ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The [full result comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) records revisions, budgets, recovery rules, and validation; EvalDash ingestion and panel visibility are verified.

The [answer review](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744559143) covers all 86 incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes. The subsequent [18-case adjudication](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744838386) records five confirmed task/reference defects, nine presentation-equivalence candidates (one with a method caveat), one submitted-answer precision error, and three unresolved reference/specification cases. Direct file checks confirm the gene-versus-record count, paired-tree aggregation, and mislabeled chromosome-length asset. A scalar/range screening pass includes all 205 outcomes and identifies cases that a blanket rounding rule would mishandle. Native grades remain unchanged; any revised task or scoring protocol must be versioned and reported separately. Fourteen other numerical/pipeline mismatches remain unresolved.

Relevant prior work: Harbor Index includes five BixBench-derived tasks. Its [merged instruction fixes](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) specify previously unstated preprocessing/modeling choices for miRNA analysis (`bix-30-q1`) and ordinal regression (`bix-10-q2`), both present in this run. Its deterministic verifiers and 20-minute budgets differ from this baseline; its audits do not validate all BixBench reference calculations.

The standalone `bixbench-verified-50@1.0` port merged in [harbor#180](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180), closing [harbor#177](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/177). It preserves all 50 questions across 33 capsules from [Phylo revision c77fc8ea](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BixBench-Verified-50/tree/c77fc8ea4611b546947b8a4710ed36ab72ee233c), credits Phylo's 17 question/answer revisions, and retains both known source defects (`bix-31-q2` and `bix-51-q8`). Existing BixBench variants and historical results are unchanged. The final [generated-task snapshot is 674c37ca8b2e](https://github.com/gonzalobenegas/harbor-datasets/tree/674c37ca8b2e537d36a1886f6cba99f2c6bdaa2f/datasets/bixbench-verified-50).

The September 21 Verified-50 run made one fresh GLM-5.3 attempt per question using Terminus-2, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, up to 16 concurrent trials, and 60-minute agent / 10-minute verifier limits. It used the disclosed 10 GiB disk override and pinned AMD64 image. The [native Harbor runtime was 17c0f88b](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/17c0f88be98b357c0c27bbf7d7e5fd6e3e6b4e8a); the later merge commit was not the solver runtime. Exact served weights remain unavailable.

Original Verified-50 outcomes were 34 correct, 1 incorrect and 15 ungraded. The separate uniform regrade produced 42 correct, 7 incorrect and 1 ungraded, preserving all 35 original grades and the saved answers. It used the JSON-schema instruction and the explicit [decimal-precision-v1 policy](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/496): 13 deterministic scalar comparisons and 36 Together GPT-OSS-120B calls, with no API errors, parsing errors or retries. GLM was not rerun. Original and intermediate results remain preserved; [archive and dashboard ingestion checks passed](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283). The curated subset and grading policy differ from the 205-question baseline, so their aggregate scores are not a controlled comparison.

The [Verified-50 seven-case audit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766975987) found no adapter mapping or extraction defect, but identified a likely false negative for the 2.18-fold answer and unresolved reference conventions. These are not seven established model errors. The unanswered `bix-49-q4` failed with exit 143 after 55.3 minutes, before the agent limit; two R workers with 48 threads each were observed on two CPUs, but termination cause remains unconfirmed. [Harbor #192](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/192) tracks grading, reference ambiguities and this R failure together. No further grade changes or R rerun have been made.

Work to track:

- [ ] Select biology benchmarks and document the capabilities each measures, its limitations, and gaps in overall coverage. MMLU biology, BixBench CLI and BixBench-Verified-50 have initial baselines; additional non-agentic benchmarks remain to be selected, and ID/OOD assignments remain undetermined.
- [x] Establish the first Harbor-based biology evaluation, recording the benchmark variant, agent harness, and grading protocol. BixBench CLI baseline completed; result and limitations summarized above.
- [ ] Address integration gaps for selected benchmarks, including reusable configurations, launchers, scoring, and Eval Dash visibility.
- [x] Adopt the BixBench verifier JSON-schema instruction: [harbor#174](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/174) merged at `b78a0e52af98015fc8416d5bd5ee649a284e5a4c`, closing [harbor#166](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/166). The Verified-50 adapter bundles this revision; formatting repair does not establish numerical equivalence.
- [ ] Regenerate or explicitly patch existing BixBench registry tasks when adopting the JSON fix, with recorded task revisions. The template change does not alter historical snapshots.
- [x] Port Phylo's Verified-50 as a separate benchmark and complete its 50-question GLM-5.3 run, uniform saved-answer regrade and seven-case review. [harbor#180](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180) is merged; final results and protocol are recorded above.
- [ ] Resolve Verified-50 grading/reference ambiguities, the two retained source defects and the unanswered R task in [harbor#192](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/192). Preserve the 42-correct / 7-incorrect / 1-ungraded result; separately scope any policy change, source repair or diagnostic rerun. [Evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766975987).
- [x] Review all 86 incorrect answers and 18 ungraded outcomes in the full BixBench run; [findings and evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744559143) distinguish observed analysis differences, reference/precision caveats and unscored failures.
- [x] Complete the evidence review of 11 precision/representation and 7 question/reference cases; [18-row decision table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744838386), reproducible file checks, and seven local upstream-report drafts are available. No grades were changed.
- [ ] Review benchmark corrections in [harbor#167](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/167), which contains all 18 cases, source revisions, reproduction details, and upstream decisions. Resolve the three remaining specifications (`bix-11-q5`, `bix-22-q6`, `bix-43-q4`) and define per-task numerical tolerances. Validate any revised scoring policy across all 205 outcomes, including existing passes, before reporting a separate result.
- [ ] Review Harbor Index's instruction fixes for `bix-30-q1` and `bix-10-q2` when specifying a corrected benchmark version; retain the original baseline protocol.
- [ ] Resolve the remaining 14 numerical/pipeline mismatches and document consequential reference preprocessing before selecting controlled reruns. Investigate missing-answer behavior and sandbox worker limits separately; exit-137 causes remain unconfirmed.
- [ ] Evaluate reference models and Snowball checkpoints under comparable protocols.
- [ ] Track results with model identity, task and evaluator revisions, per-task scores, coverage, failures, and aggregation rules so comparisons remain interpretable.
- [x] Complete the first GLM-5.3 MMLU biology evaluation and verify scores, full coverage, and Eval Dash ingestion.
- [x] Publish the initial biology-task configuration and runner on a branch, with code permalinks.

MMLU biology baseline (September 18, 2026):

GLM-5.3 was evaluated on three MMLU subjects on September 18, 2026. `MMLU-biology` names this selection: `mmlu_college_biology`, `mmlu_high_school_biology`, and `mmlu_medical_genetics`.

| Subject | Correct / questions | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| College biology | 117 / 144 | 81.25% |
| High-school biology | 267 / 310 | 86.13% |
| Medical genetics | 78 / 100 | 78.00% |

All 554 questions were evaluated using Marin's five-shot answer-choice likelihood protocol, seed 42, and no item cap. The existing Eval Dash aggregate is **81.79%**, averaging the three subject accuracies equally. Accuracy across individual questions is **83.39% (462/554)**. No unanswered items or infrastructure errors were recorded; an audit of the native outputs reproduced every grade. [EvalDash run — Marina access required](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647).

MMLU code references:

- [Biology task configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/mmlu-biology.yaml).
- [GLM-5.3 runner adapted from the completed evaluation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/experiments/evaluation/glm53_mmlu_biology.py).
- [Integration changes and usage documentation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491).
- [Marin MMLU configuration at the run's base revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3071922e5d29f3dd0f924ca0881d71fbe5c7fca9/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/mmlu.yaml#L1-L6).
- [Marin's Evalchemy configuration builder at the same revision](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3071922e5d29f3dd0f924ca0881d71fbe5c7fca9/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L197-L244).
- [Pinned Evalchemy revision used for the evaluation](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/412ae9c29c0f261581181f8668dc316a2144f0c7).

The reusable runner is an adaptation of the completed experiment; its commit is not the original run’s source revision. The exact model weights revision was unavailable, and the dataset revision followed the evaluator defaults; those limitations should accompany comparisons with future runs.

🤖 BixBench CLI development check: the explicit 10 GiB retry ran through the agent phase, but produced no scored answer. The initial attempt had been blocked before model inference because the task's default 20 GB disk request exceeded the Daytona account's 10 GB per-sandbox cap.

The retry used `environment.override_storage_mb: 10240`, following a [previous Harbor canary that hit the same limit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/75#issuecomment-5461786985). Development outcome:

- Sandbox setup completed. The agent ran for its original 3,600-second budget without creating `/workspace/answer.txt`.
- BixBench's unchanged verifier returns without writing a reward when the answer file is missing. Harbor recorded `RewardFileNotFoundError`; no Together judge decision was produced. The canonical record reports **1 attempted, 0 scored**. This is not a judged incorrect answer or a benchmark accuracy estimate.
- The end-of-agent filesystem diagnostic reported **25.7 MiB used and 9.97 GiB available** in the 10 GiB allocation. No disk-exhaustion failure was observed. This is a final filesystem reading, not peak usage or the base image's total size, and it does not establish that every capsule fits.

Protocol:

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed 205 fresh BixBench CLI attempts: **101 correct / 187 graded (54.01%)**, with **18 ungraded**. Grading coverage is **91.22%**. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is **43.79–63.43%**; 54.01% is the accuracy among graded questions.

All 177 valid native grades were retained. Eleven saved answers whose verifier calls failed with HTTP 503 received one additional grading attempt each, with the original SDK retry policy. Ten obtained grades (eight correct, two incorrect); one still failed with a provider error. No solver was rerun or answer edited. The original run and its artifacts remain preserved.

The 18 ungraded outcomes are:

- 14 missing answer/reward files following the 3,600-second agent limit.
- Two sandbox processes killed with exit 137 (`TmuxBatchProtocolError`); the cause is unconfirmed.
- One Daytona HTTP 502 gateway failure.
- One unresolved judge server error (`bix-10-q2`).

Three other trials reported `AgentTimeoutError` but produced valid verifier results; those grades remain included. Missing grades are excluded from the accuracy denominator and shown separately. The original private exporter mistakenly required 100% grading coverage; its incomplete record is preserved. The derived result applies [Marin's standard 90% completion gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py), consistent with the reporting policy in #9193. The original sample export displayed missing rewards as incorrect; the derived archive preserves all 18 as ungraded.

Protocol: `bixbench-cli@1.5`, Harbor `7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a`, task revision `711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73`, Terminus-2, 16 concurrent trials, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, and 3,600-second agent / 600-second verifier limits. The judge was Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with the original comparison prompt and 1,024-token cap. The [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800) applied to every task; numerical tolerances were unchanged. The [previously documented](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5742640265) 10 GiB disk override, pinned AMD64 image, and task-manifest hash were retained.

Validation checked all 205 task identities, sample counts against aggregate scores, all retained native grades, and the eleven selected recovery cases. Two archived trajectories were also compared byte-for-byte through the dashboard API. This establishes an exploratory CLI baseline; ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The replacement judge, missing grades, known precision caveat from the pilot, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons with other protocols. Next: review full-run scientific errors and compare future models under this same recorded protocol.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Reviewed all 86 recorded incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes from the [completed BixBench CLI baseline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667), using saved answers/trajectories and the archived reference notebooks where available. No solver or judge calls were rerun. The result remains **101/187 correct (54.01%), with 18/205 ungraded**.

Each incorrect answer has a primary review category:

| Category | Questions | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Observed analysis or protocol divergence | 54 | Identified differences in statistic, counting unit, filtering, cohort, model or enrichment workflow. Some choices are underspecified in the question; these are not all established scientific mistakes. |
| Answer precision or representation review | 11 | Submitted values may differ through rounding or units; this does not establish 11 false negatives. |
| Question or reference adjudication | 7 | Contradictory targets, unclear counting/aggregation, or unresolved reference-data provenance. |
| Numerical or pipeline mismatch unresolved | 14 | Insufficient evidence to isolate the cause without reconstructing more of the reference pipeline. |

The review ledger records a finding, confidence level, trace evidence and pinned reference capsule for each of the 104 nonpassing outcomes. Original trajectories remain in the existing evaluation archive; the detailed review ledger is retained with the private evaluation handoff. The categories above are follow-up queues, not a corrected accuracy estimate.

Concrete analysis findings:

- `bix-61-q1`: reported **4,818 discarded read pairs across two samples**. The MDR trimming log reconstructs the reference's **344,895 discarded individual reads** exactly: 334,988 forward-only survivors + 1,075 reverse-only survivors + 2 × 4,416 fully dropped pairs. Both the counting unit and sample scope changed.
- `bix-28-q4` and `bix-45-q5`: substituted a different statistic. The former used terminal-branch means grouped by species instead of per-tree long-branch scores; the latter used BUSCO score/cutoff instead of [PhyKIT relative composition variability](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/tutorials/pages/01-summarizing-information-content.html).
- `bix-16-q1/q3`: raw Chronos scores were used without the reference's sign reversal. `bix-20-q1/q3`: unclassified variants entered the denominator; the reference excludes them, giving 13/14 and 35/37. These differences are visible in the [essentiality reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-bda54b38-9b49-4009-aad6-d5f52675438a.zip), cell 34, and [variant reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-2ccdbe37-0a92-47b5-9bab-fa8a8c470799.zip), cell 18.
- RNA-seq failures repeatedly differed in count normalization, outlier exclusion, covariates, nominal versus adjusted p-values, enrichment gene lists and background. For example, the [JBX13 reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-1d54e4a7-8b0f-4224-bd31-efcfded0d46c.zip) removes three samples and models replicate, strain and medium; several answers retained all samples and omitted replicate. The [UBE2M reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) removes KL3/WL3 before enrichment, unlike the `bix-53-q6` answer. Exact contributions were not isolated through reruns.
- `bix-10` / `bix-29` severity questions also expose a reference-definition caveat: the [reference preprocessing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-fbe0e950-76f2-4eb7-a216-a2d377970922.zip), cell 17, aggregates all adverse events per participant, although questions call the endpoint COVID severity. COVID-specific/event-level alternatives therefore need protocol adjudication.

Grading and reference findings:

- `bix-19-q2` is a calculation-versus-submission example: the agent computed **Cohen's d = 0.216284**, independently matching [reference cell 30](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip), but submitted approximately **0.22**. That final answer falls outside the target interval **0.215–0.217**. Other precision candidates include 35.34% versus 35% and 5.23 versus 5.2. The 11 cases are `4-q1/q5/q6`, `11-q1/q2/q5`, `19-q2`, `28-q6`, `38-q1/q3`, and `54-q5`, all with prefix `bix-`. Tiny nonzero p-values are not automatically equivalent to literal zero; `54-q5` also has a model-input difference alongside its ratio/fraction representation.
- `bix-53-q4` has a confirmed malformed target: the question requests a **pathway count**, but the [original ideal answer](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) is **4.25E-04**. [Reference cell 79](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) explicitly counts **2** pathways. The submitted answer was **1**, so fixing the target would not automatically make it correct.
- `bix-31-q2` contradicts its stated analysis. The target interval **−0.45 to −0.35** conflicts with **abs(LFC)>0.5**. [Reference cells 32–38](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) show FAM138A at baseMean **0.483698**, unshrunk LFC **−0.383938**, and shrunk LFC **−0.060666**. The target matches the unshrunk, low-expression row despite instructions requiring shrinkage and baseMean>10. The agent answered `NA`.
- `bix-52-q1` has a reference-data bug: [reference cell 14](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) downloads **JD_Chromosome_Length.csv** into **ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv**. The agent's **1.52** ratio is internally consistent with the supplied lengths and site counts; the provenance of the target **0.47–0.67** remains unresolved. `bix-52-q5` also counts repeated records instead of distinct sites, so this data caveat does not explain all CpG failures.
- The remaining four primary adjudication cases are `bix-8-q6` (260 unique genes versus 680 transcript records; [reference cell 21](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-48a6b469-9c9d-4bef-b5b4-f29b7d6fa046.zip) counts rows), `bix-38-q6` (median of paired ratios versus ratio of group medians), `bix-43-q4` (8/514 DE genes versus 8/49 pathway genes), and `bix-22-q6` (the origin of the 0.3–0.4 correlation target was not established). These require explicit definitions or reference reconstruction.
- `bix-54-q4` additionally has reversed target interval bounds, but its submitted p-value lies outside even the sorted interval. This metadata defect does not rescue that answer.

The [verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) asks an LLM for binary equivalence. It has **no separate global numerical-tolerance rule**; some targets contain explicit intervals. The JSON-schema repair changes response format, not this comparison prompt. Before any rescoring, define a consistent precision/adjudication policy and preserve the present native grades as a separate baseline.

The 14 missing-answer traces show long model fits, repeated workbook inspection, unresolved analysis choices, and sensitivity checks after intermediate results existed. More time alone is not a demonstrated fix. The two exit-137 cases show killed statistical processes; excessive worker creation is a plausible contributor, but an OOM cause is unconfirmed. One gateway failure and `bix-10-q2`'s persistent judge 503 remain ungraded. The latter has a saved answer outside its target interval, but no manual grade was substituted.

Next: adjudicate the flagged question/reference and precision cases; document the intended analysis protocols; then select a small set of failures for any separately approved controlled rerun. Keep any revised scoring or solver results separate from this baseline. The existing verifier JSON-format PR follow-up remains open.

Reference links above use dataset revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; notebook cell indices are zero-based. Several phylogenetic and genomic-pipeline capsules contain no reference notebook, which limits causal conclusions for the 14 unresolved cases.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Agent-runtime summary for the [completed 205-question BixBench CLI run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667). Measured from each original Harbor trial’s `agent_execution.started_at` and `finished_at`; all 205 have both timestamps.

The median agent runtime was **5.6 minutes per question**. The middle 50% took **1.7–15.5 minutes**, and the 90th percentile was **37.3 minutes**.

| Questions | n | Median, min | 25th–75th percentile, min | 90th percentile, min | Mean, min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All attempted questions | 205 | 5.6 | 1.7–15.5 | 37.3 | 12.8 |
| Solver completed without interruption | 185 | 4.7 | 1.6–13.8 | 20.5 | 8.6 |
| Final grade: correct | 101 | 2.3 | 0.9–9.2 | 17.3 | 6.9 |
| Final grade: incorrect | 86 | 8.1 | 2.8–14.8 | 26.5 | 12.3 |

These are elapsed solving times, including model responses, command execution, waits and tool/network latency during the agent phase. They exclude separately timed sandbox setup, agent setup and grading. Quantiles use linear interpolation at `(n−1)×p`.

**17/205 tasks (8.3%) reached the configured 3,600-second agent cap**: 14 had no submitted answer and remained ungraded; 3 retained gradeable answers. The other three interrupted agents had two process-kill failures and one gateway failure. Capped times measure time spent before termination, not the uncensored time required to solve those tasks. Recorded capped durations were 3,600.0–3,602.3 seconds.

The median complete trial duration, including setup, grading and teardown, was **7.3 minutes**. The interval from the first trial start to the last trial finish was **3 h 28 min 48 s**.

The 185 uninterrupted solver completions include one answer whose judge still failed. Correct/incorrect rows use final saved-answer recovery grades and retain the three scored timeouts. Runtime differences between outcome groups are descriptive; task difficulty and workflow differences confound interpretation.

The complete launcher-to-export span was **3 h 36 min 11 s**, with a cap of **16 concurrent trials**. That batch span includes setup and final export; later saved-answer judge recovery is excluded. The [existing result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) remains 101/187 correct with 18 ungraded.

Per-question times, raw timestamps, source hashes and the summary calculation are retained in the private evaluation handoff. No new evaluation or grading calls were made.

comments.body:
🤖 Completed the 18-case BixBench adjudication review. Five cases have confirmed task/reference defects; nine are candidates for accepting equivalent numerical presentations (one retains an analysis-method caveat); one is an actual submitted-answer precision error; three remain unresolved because the reference precision or analysis specification is insufficient. **Original grades remain 101/187 across 205 attempts.** No solver or judge calls were made.

The decision policy evaluates the submitted answer, respects explicit target intervals, keeps integer counts exact, and permits only justified unit/ratio conversions. Eight cases are equivalent when rounded to the reference's displayed precision, but that is a review criterion, not an adopted universal scoring rule. The submitted difference 0.05014 rounds to 0.05. | [bix-11-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-cd811ead-7887-4369-b175-05aff4223765.zip) | 35.34% → 35% | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 35.34% rounds to 35%; saved calculation is 88/249 = 35.3414%. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |

None supports target 0.3–0.4. | Specify sample set, gene filter, expression summary and whether correlation is pooled or cell-type specific; regenerate the reference from that pipeline. A factor-of-ten typo is plausible but not established, and the agent and notebook use different cohorts. |
| [bix-28-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-c66d3ed9-0a95-46be-a237-ed68498ea7f6.zip) | 5.23 → 5.2 | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 5.23 rounds to 5.2; saved calculation is 5.2282463. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-31-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) | NA → Between -0.45 and -0.35 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The capsule annotation identifies FAM138A as lncRNA. Notebook cell 26 fits batch + sex; cell 32 gives baseMean 0.483698 and unshrunk LFC -0.383938; cell 36 gives shrunk LFC -0.060666. The target -0.45 to -0.35 matches the unshrunk row, contradicting the protein-coding, baseMean >10, abs(LFC)>0.5 and shrinkage requirements. NA is defensible for exclusion. | Minimal repair: explicitly ask for the unshrunk FAM138A sex coefficient from the batch + sex model before those filters. Alternatively retain the intended filtered/shrunken task and choose an eligible gene with a regenerated target. |
| [bix-38-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 2.18-fold (fungi / animals) → 2x larger in fungi | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 2.18-fold agrees with the coarse 2x target. Recomputed ratio of full-precision group medians is 2.177433; ratio of rounded IQ-TREE report medians is 2.177509. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-38-q3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 5.22% → 5% | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 5.22% rounds to 5%; saved calculation is 13/249 = 5.2209%. | Accept only in a separately versioned policy allowing equivalence at the displayed reference precision; do not change the native grade. |
| [bix-38-q6](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-975f3e91-53b0-44b1-ac9f-20023d9c8cd0.zip) | 1.9036 → 2.178 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Independent Newick branch-length sums find 96 paired orthologs and median(fungal_length/animal_length) = 1.9036165971, matching the submission. The target 2.178 instead matches the ratio of separately rounded group medians, 3.0962/1.4219 = 2.1775089669; that uses all 249 fungal and 100 animal trees. Full-precision group medians give 2.177433, also a different estimand. | Keep the paired-ratio question; reference 1.9036165971 with a declared tolerance, or explicitly request 1.904 to three decimal places. Preserve the paired ortholog list and full-precision input calculation. |
| [bix-43-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-15ff11e5-2db1-45b6-b3a3-46bc2a74b821.zip) | 8/514 → 8/49 | **Unresolved analysis specification**. The prompt asks for the proportion of differentially expressed genes, but reference cell 65 reports the Enrichr overlap 8/49, whose denominator is pathway members. Agent 8/514 uses its DEG denominator. The notebook has 679 pre-mapping DEG rows at cell 45 and drops missing gene names at cell 53; the final distinct mapped denominator was not established. | Minimal repair: ask for the Enrichr Overlap field, explicitly defined as intersecting genes / pathway genes, and retain 8/49. If retaining the DEG-proportion wording, establish mapping/deduplication and recompute that denominator. Do not certify 514 as the reference count. |
| [bix-52-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) | Chromosome W / chromosome 1 = 1.52 → Between 0.47 and 0.67 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Packaged ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv is byte-identical to JD_Chromosome_Length.csv (SHA256 59e321ef…051b); notebook cell 14 downloads the JD file under the ZF name. Three W and 29 chr1 distinct filtered sites give 1.519930 with that supplied table. The original Zenodo ZF table gives W length 20,846,394 and chr1 length 114,020,016, yielding 0.56581364, inside the existing 0.47–0.67 interval. | Replace the mislabeled capsule asset and notebook download URL with the original ZF table (Zenodo record 12205202, MD5 b078a4dab5b677bfd0742452de6b1a17). Retain the existing target interval. Future evaluation needs the corrected input; do not retroactively penalize the agent for using the supplied file. |
| [bix-53-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) | 1 → 4.25E-04 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The original dataset ideal is 4.25E-04 for a question asking how many pathways. Notebook cell 79 explicitly counts two oxidative terms among the top twenty. The submitted one is not correct merely because the gold is malformed. | Use integer target 2 only with the notebook's intended cohort, adjusted-p filtering, shrinkage and pathway-term matching explicitly specified. The current question says p while the notebook filters padj; pin that distinction before a corrected task is released. |
| [bix-54-q5](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-9e52daf6-ca58-43e8-e732-fbac3459d295.zip) | 10:1 → Between 0.9 and 0.99 inclusive | **Presentation-equivalent candidate**. 10:1 converts to a component fraction 10/11 = 0.90909, inside 0.90–0.99. Reference cells 16/19 use rhlI/(rhlI+lasI) and yield a spline maximum at 0.9076577. The prompt asks for a ratio but the target stores a fraction. The agent selected the best tested ratio from 36 mixed-culture rows; the reference spline used 39 rows, so final-answer equivalence does not validate the method. | State that the answer is the rhlI fraction; allow an explicitly labeled equivalent mixture ratio if retaining outcome-only grading. Keep the method caveat separate. |

Evidence uses the pinned BixBench dataset `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; task links above point to the corresponding source capsule. Notebook cell numbers are zero-based. Local reproduction records include the downloaded-member SHA256 manifest, gene/correlation checks, and all 96 paired tree ratios. The corrected Zebra Finch file is available in [the original Zenodo dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/12205202).

A separate [public BixBench audit](https://github.com/Anqi-Dai/BixBench_eval/blob/6070dc293677b0ef21fa38d7ab23c5850d8799c0/env/REVIEW_REPORT.md) independently documents the 680-record/260-gene mismatch. Its study covers three capsules and fourteen questions; it does not validate this entire run.

The proposed precision rule was also screened against **all 205 saved outcomes, including the 101 previously correct answers**. This was a conservative scalar/range screen, not a complete semantic regrade: 81 answers require semantic parsing, and counts, unit conversions, reversed ranges and the zero p-value need explicit treatment. It flags two existing passes that a naive comparator would reject: `bix-18-q5` supplies 0.29 against a percent-scale 25–30 target, and `bix-45-q1` supplies 7.70e-54 against 7.6968e-54. The latter needs symmetric handling of reported precision, rather than always requiring the target's extra digits. These findings block adopting a blanket rounding rule or publishing a selectively corrected accuracy.

Harbor Index provides relevant prior work: its public index includes five BixBench-derived tasks, with eighteen trials each. [Its Jackdaw notes](https://hub.harborframework.com/tasks/harbor-index/bix-cpg-density-jackdaw/latest) explicitly say the scientific derivation was not re-audited. Later [PR #142](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) fixed underspecified instructions for two tasks present in this run: miRNA analysis `bix-30-q1` ([issue #97](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/97)) and ordinal regression `bix-10-q2` ([issue #113](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/113)). The fixes specify preprocessing/modeling choices while retaining the targets. These are useful precedents for task repair, not grounds for changing our recorded grades. The index uses its own 1,200-second budgets and deterministic numeric verifiers; its results are not directly comparable to this baseline.

Next: review the seven local upstream-report drafts; agree on versioned task repairs and numerical tolerances; then validate any revised grader across all 205 outcomes before publishing a separate result. The fourteen other numerical/pipeline discrepancies and ungraded outcomes remain follow-ups. The main issue table records **per-question agent time**, with no total-duration column.

🤖 September 21 with `/nothink` now has a completed original-task baseline: one attempted, one graded, zero correct on `bix-51-q2`. It executed the analysis but excluded PD patients from the response coding. The synthetic pilot has 31 accepted teacher traces. No biology SFT or full 50-question student evaluation has run.

<details>
<summary>Checkpoint, smoke findings, and next steps (September 22, 2026)</summary>

- Full `/nothink` baseline completed: `snowball-sep21-bix51-nothink-20260922-203145` produced one graded answer and zero correct answers on unchanged `bix-51-q2`. The student submitted AIC **73.5366**; the published reference interval is **111.8–111.82 inclusive**. Agent execution took **109.9 seconds**, with 10 responses, 12 shell commands, and three parsing errors that it recovered from. This is one attempt on one task, not a full BixBench score or a pass-rate estimate.
- Method review: the student first referenced a nonexistent `PR` column, then repaired that error by using `Efficacy`. It mapped PR to 1 and SD to 0; PD became missing and was dropped, reducing the fit from 80 data-bearing rows to 58. It fitted an intercept-plus-BMI logistic model on those 58 rows and reported that model's AIC. The observed failure is response coding and cohort selection; `/nothink` enabled useful task execution but did not eliminate all formatting errors. The existing 31 accepted teacher traces use explicit binary `Groups` and do not directly exercise PR/SD/PD recoding.
- Protocol and artifacts: September 21 revision `a23aa7bbc864a73970a3dd9e499168c45d37f497`, native inference template with `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`, eight H100s, Harbor `d072bef08e54050880b484eb81d892944d1d82fb`, Marin `12bbd5d45b1b176167ab3cfe905e06004c2f02e3`, vLLM `f0d7cc7f587482e0ab771e3c9715e726eb914e60`. Same task bytes and sampling defaults, one attempt, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, and original one-hour agent / ten-minute verifier budgets. `record.json`, `results/summary.json`, `results/audit.json`, native artifacts, and provenance are saved under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/snowball-sep21-bix51-nothink-20260922-203145/`. Trajectory SHA256: `9e80df0369517c06c553d91ffa53761aa7afa918a620955119ff615774680420`.
- Export recovery and cleanup: Harbor completed and graded the saved answer before the orchestrator failed while serializing a nested configuration field. The record was recovered from those saved artifacts, validated with the experiment's pinned schema, and read back with matching hashes. `results/export-recovery.json` documents the repair; no solver or judge was rerun. The canonical evaluation status is `succeeded` with reward 0; the original Iris orchestrator remains `failed`. Both old diagnostic annotations were also serialized as strings to satisfy the same schema, with their null grades preserved. The GPU worker is terminal and the owned Daytona sandbox is confirmed absent. Dashboard ingestion has not yet been verified.

Consider adding fresh siblings requiring PR-versus-non-PR coding, then finish GPU checkpoint-conversion validation and the eight-H100 training configuration. All generated tasks remain one training split; the original data and answer remain excluded from training. No biology SFT has run.

- Update after maintainer guidance: [the release announcement](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1551990054682099794) states that September 21 includes explicit Terminus training, and [the addendum](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1355318637854199848/1552024155959066787) recommends trying `/nothink`, because Terminus already requests reasoning in `analysis` and `plan`. The earlier smoke used default `/think`.
