comments.body:
## Numeric-aware tokenizer variant update

The `*-place-digits` variants currently differ from their corresponding normal `gpt-oss` / `llama` variants only in numeric pretokenization before BPE training.

The three numeric-specific changes are:

1. **Digit-run isolation**: contiguous Unicode numeric runs are separated from surrounding text before the normal tokenizer pretokenizer runs. Example: `abc1234567def` is handled as `abc | 1234567 | def` before numeric chunking.
2. **Right-to-left, place-aligned 3-digit grouping**: each digit run is split from the right into groups of three, with a leading group of one or two digits if needed. Example: `1234567 -> 1 | 234 | 567`. This keeps each 3-digit token aligned to a fixed place-value block.
3. **Bounded, backtracking-safe implementation**: instead of one zero-width lookahead over arbitrary-length digit strings, the implementation caps numeric-run chunks at 510 characters, peels a leading 1-2 digit group when needed, then splits exact groups of 3. This preserves the intended place-aligned split for normal numeric runs and avoids pathological regex backtracking on very long digit strings.

Implementation reference in this branch:

- `experiments/datakit_testbed/tokenizer_sweep_20260526.py`
- `tests/datakit_testbed/test_tokenizer_sweep_20260526.py`

Paper/source rationale:

- Singh & Strouse (2024), **"Tokenization counts: the impact of tokenization on arithmetic in frontier LLMs"**: motivates right-to-left numeric grouping; they find right-to-left number tokenization substantially improves arithmetic behavior. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14903
- Schmidt, Reddy, Tanner & Pinter (2025), **"Boundless Byte Pair Encoding: Breaking the Pre-tokenization Barrier"**: uses right-to-left 3-digit numeric pretokens and gives the same `1234567 -> [1, 234, 567]` behavior. https://arxiv.org/html/2504.00178v2

Latest preliminary tokenizer-MoE validation results show the numeric-aware variants are useful for `gpt-oss`, especially at d768:

| comparison | vocab | dim | baseline all BPB | digits all BPB | delta |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gpt-oss -> gpt-oss-place-digits | 8k | d512 | 1.4006 | 1.3525 | -0.0481 |
| gpt-oss -> gpt-oss-place-digits | 8k | d768 | 1.1432 | 1.1134 | -0.0298 |
| gpt-oss -> gpt-oss-place-digits | 32k | d512 | 1.4418 | 1.3652 | -0.0766 |
| gpt-oss -> gpt-oss-place-digits | 32k | d768 | 1.1705 | 1.1051 | -0.0654 |
| llama -> llama-place-digits | 8k | d512 | 1.4729 | 1.4852 | +0.0123 |
| llama -> llama-place-digits | 8k | d768 | 1.2196 | 1.2203 | +0.0007 |
| llama -> llama-place-digits | 32k | d512 | 1.4656 | 1.4277 | -0.0379 |
| llama -> llama-place-digits | 32k | d768 | 1.2076 | 1.1751 | -0.0325 |

Interpretation: this is a promising signal for explicit numeric pretokenization, especially for GPT-OSS-family tokenizers and 32k vocabularies. The 8k Llama-family result is neutral/slightly worse in this preliminary train50B tokenizer-MoE table, so we should keep the numeric-aware arm as an explicit sibling variant rather than silently replacing the default tokenizer.

## TL;DR

We completed a mixed-domain RLVR campaign for Snowball 67B-A2B: a September 11 SFT policy trained through RLVR1 and RLVR2 under synchronous and bounded-staleness asynchronous schedules, plus an RLVR1 arm starting from the older 5.7T Agentic checkpoint. RLVR1 produced clear early learning, but RLVR2 validation was flat to regressing; several weak domains were also starved by non-finalizing generations, verifier/output-contract mismatches, and—on the early async lineage—local inference-bridge overload. The runs are sealed, the retained checkpoints and full releasable artifact corpus are public, and the analysis links below preserve the operational caveats needed to interpret them.

![Snowball RLVR campaign histories](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Mixed-RLVR-Experiment-Artifacts/resolve/main/06-analysis-and-reports/figures/issue-summary-campaign-history.png)

## Experiment

- Model: Snowball 67B-A2B MoE, Megatron backend.
- Data: mixed-domain RLVR1 followed without shuffling by RLVR2.
- Main comparison: synchronous RLOO-N versus bounded-staleness asynchronous RLOO-N with TIS, router replay, and TITO.
- Context: 32K model context and 6,528 generated tokens per turn for the completed arms.
- Scale: 64 H100s per training arm; batch size 512 and 16 samples per prompt.
- Completed histories: September 11 sync through cumulative step 160, September 11 async through step 146, and 5.7T Agentic RLVR1 through step 46.

The exact training-pass@16 peaks in RLVR2 were sync step 118 and async step 140. Those two checkpoint directories had already been removed by checkpoint pruning and the backing bucket had no recoverable object versions. The released RLVR2 models are therefore the best complete retained checkpoints: sync step 116 and async step 146. This distinction is recorded in their model cards and the artifact package.

## Results

- Both September 11 lineages learned during RLVR1, then failed to improve holdout validation during RLVR2.
- The asynchronous lineage is not a clean algorithm-only comparison: its early history includes local inference-bridge overload and a changed holdout denominator after LiveCodeBench was removed from the verification loop.
- The 5.7T Agentic arm reached step 46 with training reward/pass@16 0.6791/0.6875 and 100-row holdout avg_score/pass@1 0.5606/0.5000.
- Per-domain trace analysis found nearly all-zero groups in several weak domains. NVARC and structured-output verifiers had output-contract mismatches; many Lean, coding, math, and NVARC generations also failed to reach a final answer before the turn cap.

## Public artifacts

- [Complete releasable artifact corpus](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Mixed-RLVR-Experiment-Artifacts)
- [Reproduction data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-RLVR1-Repro-Data)
- [Animated RLVR1 reward by domain](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/benjaminfeuer/snowball-rlvr1-domain-reward-trends/2026.09.22/index.html)
- [10T Mixed RLVR model collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/open-athena/10t-mixed-rlvr-6aae99014a43a3fea0982366)
- [5.7T Mixed RLVR model collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/open-athena/57t-mixed-rlvr-6ab2c1be7e68576539629758)
- [Checkpoint-export S3 throttling incident](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/509)

## Released models

- [September 11 sync RLVR1, step 92](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92)
- [September 11 async RLVR1, step 92](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Async-Step92)
- [September 11 sync RLVR2, retained step 116](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR2-Sync-Step116)
- [September 11 async RLVR2, retained step 146](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR2-Async-Step146)
- [5.7T Agentic RLVR1, step 38](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-5.7T-Mixed-RLVR-Step38)

The exact step-timing report and complete arm tracker are attached as comments below. This issue is the durable experiment index for the sealed campaign.

# STEP_TIMING_REPORT

Generated 2026-09-16T02:55:29+00:00 from W&B histories. Resume overlaps are clipped to one explicit checkpoint lineage per arm.

## Schedule contract

The intended Ultra-style schedule is **RLVR1 steps 1–128 (128 updates), then RLVR2 steps 129–178 (50 updates)**. The campaign's 20-stable-step rule is an execution-verification gate, not permission to end RLVR1. Every live arm starts from the same Snowball base checkpoint, and no RLVR2 arm may launch before its matching RLVR1 step-128 checkpoint is complete.

| stage | input checkpoint | cumulative step range | stage updates | placement | intended status |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| RLVR1 (each arm) | Snowball base | 1–128 | 128 | 4 learner + 4 inference nodes | active |
| RLVR2 (each arm) | matching completed RLVR1 step 128 | 129–178 | 50 | 4 learner + 4 inference nodes | blocked on matching completed RLVR1 |

## What actually differs

All geometry, batching, data order, clipping, and rollout settings are locked across the four arms. The table below isolates the three learning-hyperparameter differences.

| live arm | learning rate | entropy coefficient | Adam beta2 | shared settings |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| AdamW 4e-6 control | 4e-6 | off | 0.999 | split 4 learner + 4 inference nodes; TP1/PP2/CP1/EP16; packed RLOO-N; BS512/GS16 |
| AdamW 8e-6 | 8e-6 | off | 0.999 | split 4 learner + 4 inference nodes; TP1/PP2/CP1/EP16; packed RLOO-N; BS512/GS16 |
| AdamW 4e-6 + entropy 0.01 | 4e-6 | 0.01 | 0.999 | split 4 learner + 4 inference nodes; TP1/PP2/CP1/EP16; packed RLOO-N; BS512/GS16 |

The 4e-6/no-entropy/beta2=.999 arm is the control. Each other arm changes exactly one learning choice.

## MFU method and limitations

MFU is an analytic learner estimate, not a hardware-counter measurement. It applies 3× forward FLOPs for training to Snowball's 26-layer, hidden-2560, 256-expert/top-4 architecture with one shared expert, seven full-attention layers, and 2,048-token local attention elsewhere. The denominator is 989.5 dense BF16 TFLOP/s per H100 SXM (half of NVIDIA's sparsity-marked 1,979 TFLOP/s figure) times policy GPUs.

Two values are shown: policy-train MFU divides by `timing/policy_train`; end-to-end MFU divides the same useful training work by `timing/step`. Both use logged average generated response length because prompt-token throughput is not logged, so they are conservative lower-bound estimates. Generation, judge work, checkpointing, and idle inference GPUs are intentionally not credited as learner FLOPs.

Hardware reference: https://www.nvidia.com/en-eu/data-center/h100/

Timing components can overlap or nest, so their means should not be summed. Cumulative wall time is the sum of logged `timing/step` values and excludes startup, queueing, failures before the first banked step, and gaps between resumes.

`timing/generate` measures the full awaited generation phase. The displayed 8,192/8,192 counter covers the individual agent loops, but the runner can then perform cohort-level reward finalization before returning. For these Ultra batches that includes GenRM cohort grading: `max_concurrent_comparisons` bounds comparisons within one cohort, while cohorts are currently graded sequentially. This closure work remains inside `timing/generate`; it has no separate timer. `timing/postprocess_trajectory_batch` and `timing/convert_to_training_input` begin only after generation returns and are independently logged.
`timing/sync_weights` accumulates every policy-to-inference synchronization in the step. On checkpoint steps, runs synchronize once after the optimizer update and again after the checkpoint temporarily backloads policy state, so the reported value includes both transfers.

Follow-up to [MarinSkyRL #732](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/732) and Marin #9345.

MarinSkyRL #732 changes the rollout default to `enforce_eager: false`, but Marin currently pins `MarinSkyRL` at `6b981f54b3cbdc9c60493bc76d6090ff678229fd`. Merging #732 alone will not change the SkyRL code installed by Marin. Marin #9345 explicitly sets Iceball rollouts to non-eager mode, but other Marin consumers will still use the old SkyRL default until the pin advances.

Done when:

- After #732 merges, update `config/external/MarinSkyRL/uv.lock` and regenerate `lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py` to pin the merged revision.
- Verify that a representative Marin SkyRL launch resolves the new revision and uses `enforce_eager: false` by default; retain explicit eager only where a model-specific reason exists.
- Record the tested Marin and MarinSkyRL revisions, then close this issue.

This is an activation follow-up, not a blocker for #9345, which already merged.

spillover_issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
spillover_issues.body:
A CPU job submitted to `marin` with `--reserve H100` fails at submission, although both H100 peers are reachable. This blocks automatic placement on an H100 cluster without allocating a GPU.

Reproduce:

1. From a Marin checkout with a prepared environment, submit a CPU-only dummy job:

```bash
uv run --no-sync iris --cluster marin job run \
  --no-wait --no-sync --exclude '.*' \
  --reserve H100 --cpu 0.1 --memory 1GB --disk 1GB \
  --timeout 180 --max-retries 0 \
  --job-name reserve-h100-probe-$(date +%s) \
  -- /bin/echo reserve-h100-probe-ok
```

2. Replace `--reserve H100` with `--target-cluster cw-rno2a` and use a new job name.
3. Inspect the returned job ID with `uv run --no-sync iris --cluster marin job describe <job-id>`. The control completes on the H100 peer.

Expected: `--reserve H100` alone permits federation to a suitable H100 peer without allocating a GPU or requiring a named cluster.

Observed on live `marin` at 2026-09-22 23:43 UTC, with CLI checkout `1e5c2f4c9e`:

```text
Job /rav/reserve-h100-probe-20260922-a is unschedulable: no scaling group matches all constraints.
constraint coverage across 82 group(s):
  preemptible==false: 19/82 satisfy
  availability:h100 exists: 0/82 satisfy
```

The rejected submission created no job. The [control job](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frav%2Freserve-h100-pin-control-20260922-a) completed with exit code 0. The `marin` controller's `federated_jobs` row confirms `peer_id=cw-rno2a`. Neither submission requested a GPU.

`uv run --no-sync iris --cluster marin rpc controller list-peers` supplies the peer advertisements.

The code at the linked revision is consistent with the live failure. The deployed controller revision was not recorded:


- `--reserve H100` adds `availability:h100 EXISTS`, which `routing_constraints` retains for peer matching. [constraints.py:1058](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1e5c2f4c9eb3e2f0d814d3907cca2e47d008e982/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/constraints.py#L1058-L1078)
- Live `ListPeers` showed both `cw-rno2a` and `cw-us-east-02a` reachable, with `device-variant=h100`, but no `availability:h100`. `backend_attribute_sets` emits device and region attributes. [config.py:1222](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1e5c2f4c9eb3e2f0d814d3907cca2e47d008e982/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/config.py#L1222-L1231)
- `_peer_can_host` requires every routing constraint to match. `EXISTS` fails when the attribute is absent. These peers also omit `preemptible`. In this code, that independently rejects the default `preemptible==false` constraint for small CPU jobs. [router.py:67](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1e5c2f4c9eb3e2f0d814d3907cca2e47d008e982/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/router.py#L67-L99)

An explicit cluster pin bypasses this submit-time peer check. [router.py:116](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1e5c2f4c9eb3e2f0d814d3907cca2e47d008e982/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/router.py#L116-L124)

Related: #7099 tracks numeric free-GPU capacity. This failure concerns placement-only CPU jobs. Found during review of #9287.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Research

`--reserve H100` adds a hard availability constraint. The [peer attributes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c287d85649a27a2c2ddf54d49120e6192ebbea90/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/config.py#L1222-L1231) omit availability and preemptibility, so the [submit router](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c287d85649a27a2c2ddf54d49120e6192ebbea90/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/federation/router.py#L81-L99) rejects the CPU job. The queue placement pass uses the same attribute matcher. The open-PR check found no implementation overlap. #9287 changes experiment code.

Proposed Fix

Add configured accelerator availability and preemptibility to peer attributes. Keep numeric GPU capacity separate, so a CPU job with `--reserve H100` does not reserve GPUs. Add regression tests through peer heartbeat, submit classification, and queue placement, with rejection cases for incompatible peers. Update the federation documentation.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 The fix is in [PR #9356](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9356). Peer attributes include configured accelerator availability and preemptibility, so CPU reservations can route to suitable peers without GPU allocation or a cluster pin.

The regression failed before the fix and passes after it. Lint and type checks pass. The affected suite had 4,723 passes, six Tasktrove failures that also reproduce on `main`, and one Grug timeout that passes alone.

The lint-catalog review suggested a helper for the scalar preemptibility comparison. The comparison stays inline because a helper adds indirection without consolidating an algorithm. CI and review monitoring will continue on the PR.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 The docs and test cleanup is in commit 31c91ac72. It removes 80 lines and keeps the H100 regression, wrong-variant rejection, and preemptible-only rejection. All 117 affected tests, lint, and type checks pass.

The live check at 2026-09-23 03:18 UTC still rejects `--reserve H100`. Both H100 peers omit `availability:h100` and `preemptible`, so this check cannot validate the fix before a peer controller deployment.

The [pinned control job](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Frav%2Fissue-9354-pin-control-31c91ac72) completed on `cw-rno2a` with exit code 0. It requested 0.1 CPU, 1 GB memory, 1 GB disk, and no GPU.

No controller changed. Deployment preflight found no Docker or CoreWeave storage credentials in this session. The live regression test awaits a deployment-capable session and approval for a controller-only rollout to `cw-rno2a`.

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
PR #9289 exposed a family of launch, lifecycle, storage, and data-integrity
failures while running a bounded Snowball drafting benchmark. This issue is the
current catalog. Older comments retain the incident chronology; the lists below
describe the current state.

## Fixed and merged

- **Remote model and checkpoint I/O.** [MarinSkyRL
  #715](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/715) mirrors pinned
  Hugging Face revisions once, keeps policy and draft weights on S3, gives vLLM
  manifest-backed S3 locators, lets Megatron read rank-owned safetensor ranges,
  and streams native Megatron checkpoint reads and writes. It replaces the
  complete-model-per-task staging diagnosed in MarinSkyRL #713.
- **Iris setup recovery.** [Marin
  #9322](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9322) recovers from a
  corrupt shared `uv` cache in the same attempt and gives direct and brokered
  inference jobs a failure budget consistent with their retry count.
- **Unsafe rank-local rendezvous retry.** [vLLM
  #74](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/pull/74) stops one data-parallel
  rank from silently switching ports while its peers wait on the original
  rendezvous.

## Fixed in open changes

- [Marin #9289](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9289) makes
  `skyrl_step` return `SkyRLRun` without exporting by default; represents the HF
  URI as optional; makes `skyrl_smoke` use an evaluation-only entrypoint; places
  the federated root and its children consistently; gives evaluation descendants
  matching retry budgets; reconstructs native Evalchemy prompts; rejects partial
  or assistant-only SFT corpora; isolates retry environments from mutable shared
  caches; and honors latest-versus-best draft-checkpoint selection. It also
  contains the checked-in bounded Snowball experiment exercising these paths,
  pins capture and serving to the agentic export's embedded tokenizer, and rejects
  the older stage-2 chat template for this target.
  After an overlap audit found all 14 sampled GSM8K prompts in the SFT corpus,
  the benchmark now derives its evaluation pool by excluding the SFT sources;
  the replacement pool contains 943 MATH500, AMC, reasoning-gym, TheoremQA, and
  OmniMath rows. The three source-disjoint arms completed end to end: exact-target
  SFT raised mean acceptance length from 1.5010 to 1.7100 and proposal acceptance
  from 16.70% to 23.67%.
- [MarinSkyRL
  #716](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/716) reserves one
  rendezvous configuration for a complete vLLM DP generation, inspects readiness
  references as they finish, and tears down the actor gang on the first failure.
- [MarinSkyRL
  #717](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/717) runs standard and
  TerminalBench evaluation without learners, policy workers, optimizer work, or
  checkpoints; supervises and tears down the complete runtime; and publishes
  cumulative token, throughput, and speculative-decoding metrics.
- [MarinSkyRL
  #722](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/722) bounds evaluation
  prompt counts, migrates pre-manifest S3 exports under a distributed lock,
  synthesizes missing single-shard indexes, supports policy-tokenizer reuse for
  drafts, and honors the launch request's pinned tokenizer across prompt
  construction, Harbor, export, and vLLM serving. It also keeps evaluation-only
  vLLM engines awake instead of discarding and restoring their weights before the
  first rollout; that sleep/wake cycle produced incoherent Snowball output despite
  a coherent standard-serving evaluation of the same checkpoint.

These items are implemented, and the checked-in benchmark now succeeds against
the pinned open revisions. They are not complete until the open PRs land and the
experiment pins their merged revisions.

## Remaining work

1. **Credential and capability declarations.** A workload must declare which
   Daytona credential and capabilities it needs. The coordinator should resolve
   that declaration, map it to the worker-facing `DAYTONA_API_KEY`, and reject a
   TaskTrove Dockerfile before GPU allocation when the selected account forbids
   declarative builds. Checked-in commands should not require callers to know
   internal secret names.
2. **One S3 storage profile.** Selecting an S3 artifact prefix should provide the
   coordinator and descendants with one coherent credential, endpoint, addressing,
   and conditional-write configuration. Current launches can still require
   separately supplied CoreWeave, generic AWS, `FSSPEC_S3`, and endpoint settings.
3. **Stream the offline hidden-state-capture target.** Marin's
   `capture_hidden_states` still recursively downloads the target HF export into
   task-local storage before starting its in-process vLLM server. It should reuse
   the manifest-backed S3 locator and metadata-only cache now used by MarinSkyRL;
   the merged SkyRL streaming fix does not cover this offline Marin path.
4. **Propagate one context budget through Harbor HTTP serving.** Clamp requested
   completion tokens against the remaining model context, including template
   tokens, and terminate with `stop_reason=length` when no budget remains. The
   current mismatch can turn long valid TerminalBench prompts into masked
   `ContextLengthExceededError` rewards.
5. **Make progress timeouts workload-aware.** Derive or require group-admission
   bounds from agent timeout and retry envelopes, and treat active terminal-agent
   traffic as progress. A four-trial group can validly exceed the old fixed
   1,800-second limit.
6. **Support compatible artifact-marker migration.** Provide a checked-in,
   provenance-preserving migration for zero-field `Artifact` subclasses, or fail
   planning with the exact migration command. Manually editing `.artifact.json`
   must not be the recovery path.
7. **Complete secret redaction.** Redact resolved values from `ArtifactStep` and
   `RemoteCallable` representations and from every raw job-configuration API,
   not only submitted argv and the normal status view.
8. **Make retry policy apply to the whole job tree.** Cache-corruption recovery
   should not depend on each experiment discovering every descendant submission
   layer and setting both per-task retries and cumulative job failures. Define a
   coherent default for standard and custom setup scripts.
9. **Bound coordinator launcher fan-out.** A `marin --run` entrypoint defaults
   to 1 GB, but three independent SkyRL artifact steps started three isolated
   MarinSkyRL launcher environments in that coordinator. The first process tree
   reached 48.7 GB and was OOM-killed before it submitted any GPU job. A 64 GB
   retry also OOMed while two launchers were active; it submitted replacement
   GPU jobs just before Iris terminated their failed parent. Running with
   `--max-concurrent 1` is the current safe operational setting, not the product
   fix. Reuse one launcher environment, move launchers into bounded child tasks,
   or set a workload-aware default concurrency and derive the coordinator
   resource request from it.
10. **Make distributed S3 model streaming resilient.** During one matched
    three-arm launch, the trained arm streamed the shared target successfully,
    while the control and starting-draft arms each exhausted two task attempts
    with RunAI Streamer `File access error` on individual DP ranks. The same fault
    recurred in both attempts of a later `--max-concurrent 1` launch, so
    coordinator fan-out is not the cause. RunAI model-streamer 0.16.1 is the
    latest release and has no read retry. A subsequent PR #722 run partitioned
    whole files among DP ranks and still failed with the same error, so changing
    partition policy is not a fix. The error does not name the failed object or
    byte range and the streamer does not retry the failed read. A final control
    run with `RUNAI_STREAMER_CONCURRENCY=1` succeeded: all eight DP ranks loaded
    13.9–15.8 GiB from S3 in 28–31 seconds. The three final benchmark arms then
    completed with that setting. This implicates per-rank request fan-out and
    provides a safe setting for this topology, but it is not evidence that the
    read path is resilient. Add bounded per-object or per-chunk retries with
    actionable diagnostics, and validate a safe default across topologies.
11. **Do not cache asynchronous submission as completed work.** `skyrl_step`
    recorded a successful `SkyRLRun` artifact as soon as it submitted the child
    Iris job. The child later exhausted its retries, but a fresh coordinator
    served the launch descriptor from cache and reported `already succeeded
    (pruned subtree)` without running the failed benchmark. Tie the artifact's
    completion state to the descendant job's terminal success, or invalidate the
    cached launch descriptor when that descendant fails.
12. **Generalize train/evaluation overlap enforcement.** #9289 now removes the
    known GSM8K overlap from this benchmark, but source exclusion is a local fix,
    not a reusable integrity check. Dataset construction should persist stable
    prompt IDs or normalized hashes, reject cross-artifact overlap before launch,
    and record the audit in benchmark metadata. The invalidated 64-prompt run had
    14 exact GSM8K matches; the replacement benchmark excludes every SFT source.

## Completion gate

- Merge #9289 and the required MarinSkyRL PRs, pin their merged revisions, and run
  the checked-in bounded benchmark from a clean coordinator environment.
- Before testing a draft, require a short target-only quality preflight against a
  known-good prompt. The corrected preflight confirmed parity with the coherent
  Evalchemy result for the same checkpoint after the evaluation-only sleep cycle
  was removed. Do not report acceptance or throughput when the target emits
  incoherent text or exhausts the context window.
- Verify that the smoke produces rollout, reward, response-token, throughput, and
  acceptance metrics while creating no policy checkpoint or HF export.
- Verify that serving and policy/draft checkpoint weight I/O remain remote. Until
  remaining item 3 is fixed, record the offline capture target's local staging
  explicitly rather than treating it as remote streaming.
- Close or split the twelve remaining items above into linked, owned issues; keep
  this rollup open until every item has an owner and completion evidence.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 The full drafting benchmark exposed another launch failure. One eight-rank vLLM DP group collided on port 26128; vLLM retried rank 0 alone on port 23834 while ranks 1–7 kept waiting on 26128. SkyRL then hid the failed generation behind `ray.wait(..., num_returns=len(refs))` until its 1,800-second startup timeout, holding the 96-H100 gang throughout.

The benchmark was cancelled. marin-community/vllm#74 makes multi-rank port collisions fail instead of changing one rank’s port, and marin-community/MarinSkyRL#716 tears down the actor gang on the first failed readiness reference.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 The credential contract is workload-dependent, not merely a naming mismatch. The canonical `DAYTONA_RL_API_KEY` reaches workers correctly, but the RL account rejects the TaskTrove Dockerfile with `400 declarative builds are not allowed`. All 128 agent rollouts in r11 hit that capability error. The same benchmark in r12, launched with the existing `DAYTONA_DATA_API_KEY` secret mapped to the worker-facing `DAYTONA_API_KEY`, has passed sandbox creation and is executing terminal-agent inference.

The fix should let a SkyRL workload declare which Daytona credential and capabilities it needs, then resolve that declaration at the coordinator boundary. A TaskTrove source containing an `environment/Dockerfile` must request a credential that permits declarative builds. It should not silently receive the restricted RL credential merely because the caller is an RL benchmark. Add a preflight or capability-specific error before the GPU job launches, and update the TaskTrove smoke example accordingly.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 r12 exposed a further benchmark-path mismatch. The step-wise trajectory runner clamps each request to the remaining model context, but the Harbor HTTP path forwards Terminus requests with `max_tokens=4096`. Once a clipped prompt reaches 28,673 tokens, vLLM rejects the 32,769-token total against Snowball's 32,768-token limit. Harbor classifies this as `ContextLengthExceededError` and the benchmark masks it to a zero reward, so it is bounded rather than a job hang, but it makes rollout completion and reward depend on an avoidable transport error.

The benchmark helper should propagate one context budget through the agent and HTTP serving boundary, account for generation-template tokens, clamp the requested completion length before vLLM validation, and end a trajectory with `stop_reason=length` when no budget remains. Add parity coverage against `trajectory_runners.step_wise.clamp_generation_tokens`.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 r12 also showed that SkyRL’s first-batch group-admission timeout is not workload-aware. The TaskTrove arm was still producing valid terminal-agent traffic when it failed exactly at the default 1,800 seconds with `GroupAdmissionStalledError`; a prompt group can include four trials, each with a 600-second agent timeout and bounded retries. The experiment now sets 3,600 seconds explicitly, but the benchmark API should derive or require a bound consistent with the trajectory timeout and retry envelope, and its progress detector should distinguish active production from a true admission stall.

Credential inspection has a separate redaction gap: Iris presents environment values redacted in submitted argv, but a raw job-config query can return the environment mapping unredacted. The query/API serialization path should apply the same secret-field redaction policy before returning job configuration. No credential values are included here.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 The stuck benchmark exposed a second launch-contract bug: `skyrl_smoke` disabled export callbacks but still ran the full trainer, so rollout-only measurements entered group admission, constructed policy workers, ran the optimizer, and could stall replacing unusable groups. PR #9289 now routes smoke runs through the dedicated `generate` entrypoint with validation data and an 8-node inference-only topology. MarinSkyRL PR #717 disables Ray-local retries for this entrypoint, uses the shared job supervisor, performs explicit teardown, and publishes final cumulative inference/speculation counters. r14 is exercising the corrected path on the same three agentic arms.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 The mixed-corpus draft-SFT launch exposed three more launch-contract failures.

Iris federates only root jobs. A coordinator on the hub cannot submit an H100 child to `cw-us-east-02a`; Iris rejects it with `only whole root jobs are federated to a peer`. Submitting the root to `cw-us-east-02a` also failed while the Evalchemy child retained `AcceleratorChoice.target_cluster="cw-us-east-02a"`, because that child attempted to federate from the East controller to itself. PR #9289 removes the child target and assigns East placement only to the root command. Checked-in experiment commands should express cluster placement once, and planning should reject or normalize a child target equal to the root cluster.

Running the coordinator on the hub with `MARIN_PREFIX=s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin` required four independently supplied pieces: CoreWeave credentials, generic AWS credentials, virtual-hosted `FSSPEC_S3` configuration, and `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL[_S3]` for conditional lock objects. Omitting each produced `NoCredentialsError`, `400 Bad Request`, or `InvalidAccessKeyId`. Selecting an S3 artifact prefix should inject one coherent storage profile into the coordinator and its child jobs.

`repr(ArtifactStep)` includes `RemoteCallable.env_vars` with resolved values. Inspecting one rollout step printed live W&B, Hugging Face, and OpenAI tokens. Config and step representations must redact secret environment values. The exposed tokens will be rotated; no values are included in this comment.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 The first correctly placed mixed-corpus run reached Q/A inference startup, then two workers hit malformed shared-cache wheels (`Metadata field Name not found` for pandas and NumPy). Both jobs had `max_retries_failure=1`, but `max_task_failures` remained at its independent default of zero. Iris failed each job on the first task failure, so the retry-local uv cache in PR #9322 was never used.

PR #9322 now sets the cumulative failure budget alongside the per-task retry count for direct and brokered inference jobs. The run was cancelled while the third worker was starting. The next run will include both halves of the recovery path: a private uv cache on retry and a job budget that permits the retry.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 A fresh SFT launch exposed another zero-budget layer. `/power/snowball-eagle-s3-mixed-sft-20260922-r9/run_served_evalchemy-53fdd51a` hit a corrupted cached `pandas` wheel during Iris setup and stopped after attempt 0 because the served-Evalchemy coordinator inherited `max_retries_failure=0` and `max_task_failures=0`. The root command’s `--max-retries 1` does not propagate to descendant jobs.

PR #9289 now sets one retry and a matching cumulative failure budget on the served-Evalchemy coordinator, its Evalchemy child, and the shared evaluation-batch coordinator. PR #9322 applies the same rule to direct and brokered inference workers. The remaining launch-default problem is systemic: callers must find every descendant submission layer and opt it into cache-corruption recovery. A coherent default or setup-specific retry policy should cover the whole job tree.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 Follow-up evidence from `/power/snowball-eagle-s3-mixed-sft-20260922-r12`: root setup reproduced the malformed cached pandas wheel on attempt 0, then the default setup script switched to `$IRIS_WORKDIR/.uv-recovery-cache`, reinstalled successfully, and submitted all three evaluation coordinators without consuming a task retry. PR #9322 now keeps this same-attempt fallback and the retry-attempt cache selection. The fallback works from the submitted bundle; the broader custom-setup retry policy still requires an Iris runtime rollout.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 The corrected SFT run exposed two additional integrity failures, both now fixed in PR #9289. Native Evalchemy preserved the exact chat prompt in its source JSONL but wrote prompt-less normalized sample rows; rollout normalization therefore produced 482 assistant-only GSM8K conversations while still reporting 512 rows. The evaluator runner now rebuilds canonical samples from the preserved native records before deriving rollouts. The Snowball corpus writer also rejects assistant-only rollouts and requires the exact configured conversation count, so this class of partial-data run fails before hidden-state capture or training.\n\nA separate Iris setup failure came from node-local uv caches containing inconsistent files for the same Polars 1.42.1 package. PR #9289 makes default setup copy packages instead of symlinking mutable cache contents and derives retry-local cache selection from the task attempt encoded in IRIS_TASK_ID, so it works without a controller rollout. r24 validated recovery when attempt 0 landed on a poisoned node; r25 is exercising the repaired evaluation-to-corpus path.

spillover_issues.title: [rl] Make SkyRL benchmark launches work from checked-in commands

spillover_issues.author: lukedhlee
spillover_issues.body:
Updated 2026-09-22. This top block is the current state of the thread. Each comment below is one experiment as it landed, with its own tables and figures; the original post from 2026-09-17 is kept at the bottom.

I evaluated Snowball 67B-A2B checkpoints under [Eval Policy v0.1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): harbor `7b18505a`, terminus-2 with summarization on, 32,768 / 8,192 tokens, temperature 1.0, Daytona, one trial per task. Training-side write-ups: [RL from the base](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/01897efa3ae7c474732c61d35150a43a) and [SFT then RL](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/48185da748a200d44f7fe31431054e37).

## Base vs SFT vs RL vs SFT then RL

![Base, SFT, RL and SFT then RL on SWE-bench Verified random-100 and Terminal-Bench 2](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/faabbba4c9ca4862b1043ad39d7b6df68680da2a/fig9_headline.png)

| checkpoint | SWE-bench Verified random-100 | Terminal-Bench 2 |
|---|---|---|
| base ([Stage-3 SFT](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888)) | 0.145 [0.11, 0.19] | 0.094 [0.06, 0.14] |
| SFT on OpenThoughts-Agent traces (D epoch 1: OTA-SFT-100K minus IssueTasks + RST successes + if-v2, 517 steps) | 0.241 [0.20, 0.29] | 0.061 [0.04, 0.10] |
| RL from base ([update 48](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step48), GRPO on R2E-Gym; 1 trial, 16 concurrent) | 0.25 [0.18, 0.34] | 0.103 [0.06, 0.19] |
| **SFT then RL** (D epoch 1 + 30 GRPO steps on a 939-task R2E-Gym band) | **0.307 [0.26, 0.36]** | 0.050 [0.03, 0.08] |

Pooled pass@1 over three trials at 32 concurrent, Wilson 95 % intervals; per-trial counts are in the figure. The RL-from-base row is one trial at 16 concurrent from before the setting moved to 32, so it is not paired with the other rows. TB2 denominators are scored tasks; the trials lost to infrastructure stay inside the 10 % allowance and counting them as failures does not change the order.

**Reading.**

- **SWE-bench moves at every rung.** SFT alone (0.24) reaches what RL from the base reaches at update 48 (0.25), and 30 GRPO steps on top of the SFT add another 7 points to 0.31, the best number in the thread. Each step sits outside the previous interval.
- **Terminal-Bench 2 does not move.** Nothing beats the base's 0.094. The SFT reads 3 points below base, RL shifts its start by about a point either way, and the one RL-from-base trial at 0.10 is inside the base's interval. Doubling every agent time budget changes neither benchmark (comment 3), so this is not a wall-clock effect.
- **Why the split.** R2E-Gym, SWE-smith and SWE-bench are the same work, a Python repo with failing tests to fix. Both SFT and RL teach the model to finish a repo fix inside the window: agent timeouts on SWE-bench drop from about 50 per 100 for the base to 30 to 40. The held-out RST probe (comment 2) shows the same SFT is slower on unfamiliar terminal tasks, which is what TB2 measures.
- **What to carry and what to drop.** D epoch 1 + RL is the checkpoint going forward. A second SFT epoch is not worth it (0.237 before RL, 0.267 after, with a faster-sharpening policy). SFT on Kimi SWE-smith traces before RL does not beat RL from the base (comment 1). RST rollouts without the OTA traces collapse both benchmarks (comment 2).

## Summarization helps a checkpoint trained without it

Training ran terminus-2 with summarization off at 49,152 / 16,384 tokens. Under the policy setting (32k, summarization on) the RL checkpoint scores its best number, and its lead over base is the same size with summarization on, off at 32k, and off at the training budget (+11, +5, +11). The base cannot work without summarization (94 to 97 of 100 trials overflow at either budget); RL cut that to 42 at the training budget. Keeping summarization on in v0.1 is right for this model family and is not a mismatch with how the checkpoint was trained.

<details><summary>How each SWE-bench trial ended, by terminus-2 setting</summary>

![How each SWE-bench trial ended, by terminus-2 setting](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/cac4e15e3f7d8f684aa35b7bddb24ec58bdd5042/fig6_summarization_context.png)

All 600 trials scored. The base's two summarization-off rows were served at temperature 0.7 with a repetition penalty of 1.1 by mistake; every other row is temperature 1.0 with no penalty. Agent requests set `skip_special_tokens: false` so the think markers stay in the transcript; a paired probe (23, 24 with the flag, 23 without) says it does not change the score.
</details>

## Thread map

- [Comment 1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9225#issuecomment-5742264977) (09-19): Kimi SWE-smith SFT, plain and TailSFT, then 24 RL updates. Neither beats RL from the base; the two SFT checkpoints turned out to be near-replicates, and 39 % of the Kimi traces are failed trials that declare done.
- [Comment 2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9225#issuecomment-5753734747) (09-21): four SFT arms on OTA traces, RST rollouts and if-v2, three trials each. Every OTA arm lifts SWE-bench 7 to 10 points, D (RST successes) is best by a margin inside noise, RST alone collapses, held-out probes explain the TB2 gap.
- [Comment 3](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9225#issuecomment-5765540707) (09-21): D dose curve (one third, two thirds, epoch 1, epoch 2). Most of the SWE-bench gain is in by one third of an epoch; doubled time budgets change nothing.
- [Comment 4](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9225#issuecomment-5777718831) (09-22): plain GRPO from D epoch 1 and epoch 2. 0.307 and 0.267 on SWE-bench, flat on TB2; the 939-task band, training curves and cost.
- [Comment 6](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9225#issuecomment-5786970615) (09-22): the Grug Datakit SFT from 09-21, a different base and mix, run with thinking off. 0.21 on SWE-bench in one trial, between the Stage-3 base and D + RL; about 0.07 on TB2, no better than base, like every SFT here.

## Launch configs and reproduction

Every row of the headline table has its launch record in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/d152f86a58e8619a988361e1502f9e55): the SFT stage (code branch, corpus pins, optimizer, launch line), the two RL run configs as the launcher wrote them (`skyrl_hydra_args` is the literal argv), and the Eval Policy v0.1 job file with the serving settings.

| row | what to open |
|---|---|
| SFT (D epoch 1) | marin `lukedhlee/vista-snowball-sft` @ `23d8fda7`, stage `ota3_if_rstsucc`, lr 1e-4 on a 2-epoch cosine, 16 GH200 nodes; launch line and corpus pins in the gist |
| RL from base, update 48 | `rl_from_base__snowball_ttband_ns_c_lr5e7_c.json`: 20 nodes (8 policy + 12 engine), lr 5e-7, staleness 2, no KL, 1,003-task band |
| SFT then RL | `rl_from_sft_d_epoch1__snowball_ttband_ota3d517u_a.json`: identical except the model path, the 939-task band, 30 steps, 3 warmup steps, 768 sandboxes |
| evaluation | `eval_policy_v01_terminal_bench_2.yaml` + harbor `7b18505a`; SWE-bench swaps the dataset to `DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders` `0c553bd6` |

Code: MarinSkyRL and harbor branches `lukedhlee/snowball-r2egym` in marin-community (SFT-then-RL at `a03b2773` / `dcf609bc`), vLLM `marin-community/vllm` `fa50698a` with the EAGLE-3 draft. The old-stack configs behind the original post's update-36 row are in [80ffe770](https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/80ffe7707328de9891eaf2d078dc180e). Job directories and traces are on JSC Jupiter; happy to attach any trial.

<details><summary>Original post (2026-09-17): RL from the base under the policy, update 24 vs 36 vs 48</summary>

**Checkpoints.** Base = [laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-sft-s3-nemotron-terminal-step1888). RL = GRPO on R2E-Gym repository-fix tasks with terminus-2 (terminal only), [old stack update 36](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-oldstack-step36) and [new stack update 24](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step24), the pick. Two later checkpoints are in the figure too: [update 48](https://huggingface.co/laion/snowball-67b-a2b-rl-r2egym-newstack-step48) of the same run, and update 24 continued for 24 more updates on a refreshed pool of 1,247 tasks. Training ran terminus-2 with summarization **off** at 49,152 input / 16,384 output tokens.

### 1. The RL gain is in-distribution: SWE-bench Verified moves, Terminal-Bench 2 does not

![Under Marin's eval policy, the RL gain shows on SWE-bench and not on Terminal-Bench 2](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/3998f0fb24fe70f1d6aa7d55fa575b2255bc51e9/fig5_policy_id_vs_ood.png)

Whiskers are 95% intervals, about ±8 points with one trial per task. Paired on SWE-bench the new checkpoint solves 15 tasks the base does not and loses 4 (12 to 8 against the old stack). On TB2 the base and the two RL picks are within noise and update 24 is lowest in every setting I tried. Training longer does not move SWE-bench: update 48 scores 25 against update 24's 23 and wins 13 tasks while losing 11, the same churn two identical runs of update 24 show (23 and 24, disagreeing on 22 tasks). The refreshed pool did not buy transfer: 17 on SWE-bench, losing 16 tasks to update 24 and winning 10, and 5 of 89 on TB2. The one hint of anything is update 48 on TB2, 9 of 87 against 4, winning 6 and losing 1, still inside a one-trial interval. TB2 denominators are scored tasks; 0 to 4 trials per run were lost to infrastructure (mostly the agent running `pkill -f` inside the sandbox, which kills harbor's own tmux command), inside the 10 % allowance, and counting them as failures does not change the order.

R2E-Gym and SWE-bench are the same kind of work, a Python repo with failing tests to fix, and that is where the 11 points show up. The RL checkpoint declares done fast (median 4 minutes of agent time per SWE-bench task vs 21 for the base), which is what finishing inside the window looks like on repo fixes and what giving up early looks like on TB2's long build-and-verify tasks.

### 2. Summarization helps the RL checkpoint, even though it was never trained with it

SWE-bench random-100 at the policy setting, at 32k with summarization off, and at the training setting (49k/16k, off), for base and the new checkpoint:

![How each SWE-bench trial ended, by terminus-2 setting](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/cac4e15e3f7d8f684aa35b7bddb24ec58bdd5042/fig6_summarization_context.png)

All 600 trials scored, no infrastructure losses. A trial that runs out of context stops and is graded as it stands. Caveat: the base's two summarization-off rows were served at temperature 0.7 with a repetition penalty of 1.1 by mistake; every other row is temperature 1.0 with no penalty. It cannot change the picture for a model that overflows on 97 of 100 tasks, but those two rows are not sampler-paired with the rest. Agent requests in all runs set `skip_special_tokens: false` so the think markers stay in the transcript; Marin's agentic launcher does not set this flag today. A paired probe says it does not matter for the score: the RL checkpoint at the policy setting scores 23 and 24 of 100 with the flag (two runs) and 23 without it, and the two flag-on runs disagree on as many tasks (22) as flag-on vs flag-off (23), so per-task differences are sampling noise at temperature 1.0.

- The base cannot work without summarization: 94 to 97 of 100 trials overflow at either budget. RL cut that to 42 at the training budget.
- The RL checkpoint's best number is with summarization on, which training never used, and its lead over base is the same size in every setting (+11, +5, +11). RL improved the task skill rather than fitting one context regime.
- Summarization at 32k beats a 49k window without it, for both models. 23 vs 19 is inside the one-trial noise; a 3-trial rerun (~15 GH200 node-hours) would settle it.

**Takeaways for the policy.** Keeping terminus-2's summarization on in v0.1 is the right call for this model family, and it is not a mismatch with how the checkpoint was trained. SWE-bench random-100 is the ID leg that detects R2E-Gym RL; TB2 does not, at this checkpoint.

**Reproduction.** Stack, task revisions (DCAgent2/terminal_bench_2, DCAgent2/swebench-verified-random-100-folders `0c553bd6`) and the variant configs are in the gist's "Policy evaluation" section. Job directories and traces are on JSC Jupiter; happy to attach any trial.


</details>

comments.author: lukedhlee
comments.body:
Follow-up: I put SFT in front of the same RL and it did not beat RL from the base. Same Eval Policy v0.1 setting as above (harbor `7b18505a`, one trial per task, 16 concurrent, 32,768 / 8,192 tokens, terminus-2, summarization on, Daytona). Training-side story and the SFT diagnosis: https://gist.github.com/lukedhlee/48185da748a200d44f7fe31431054e37.

**What ran.** Two SFTs of the base on Kimi K2 SWE-smith traces (standard, and "TailSFT" = the same recipe with the filtered objective of [arXiv 2608.25756](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25756): each step drops the 25 % of documents whose loss has fallen the most against their loss under the initial model, so training concentrates on what is not fit yet), each followed by 24 GRPO updates on its own learnable R2E-Gym band (the training tasks it solved 1–7 times out of 8 in a screen of the same 1,247-task pool; 454 and 453 tasks, the same count as the base's band). Same recipe as the base + RL row: lr 5e-7, staleness 2, no KL, 12 nodes per arm.

![SFT then RL, SWE-bench and TB2 under Eval Policy v0.1](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/lukedhlee/f50158cdcffb2a6367d26f63432a3f2a/raw/658683eb60aa0fc94be408b54a038f280a8c1642/fig6_sft_to_rl.png)

| checkpoint | SWE-bench Verified random-100 | Terminal-Bench 2 |
|---|---|---|
| base (SFT) | 12 / 100 | 6 / 84 |
| Kimi SWE-smith SFT | 7 / 100 | 3 / 89 |
| TailSFT | 11 / 99 | 2 / 89 |
| Kimi SWE-smith SFT + RL 24 | 20 / 100 | 5 / 89 |
| TailSFT + RL 24 | 13 / 100 | 6 / 88 |
| base + RL 24 (new stack, from above) | **23 / 100** | 4 / 87 |

### 1. RL repaired the standard SFT's regression, but only back to where RL from the base already was

The standard SFT lost 5 points to the base (7 vs 12, paired 4 wins / 9 losses). 24 RL updates took it to 20: it now solves 18 tasks the SFT could not and loses 5, and paired against the base it wins 14 / loses 6. Against base + RL 24 it is 8 / 11 with 12 shared, so inside one-trial noise of the 23 and not above it. On TB2 every row is within noise of the base's 6.

### 2. TailSFT started higher single-shot and RL barely moved it

TailSFT read level with the base before RL (11 vs 12) and had the steeper pass@k curve (25 vs 22 at pass@8 on this split). After the same 24 updates it is at 13: 5 unlocked, 3 lost against its own start, and 4 / 14 against base + RL 24. Both arms roughly doubled their training reward over the 24 updates and both learned to declare done more often (standard 32 % → 63 % of attempts, TailSFT 54 % → 80 %). The difference is what happened underneath: the standard SFT arm's pass@8 on its training batches rose from .69 to .84, while the TailSFT arm's stayed flat at about .74 and its reward came from finishing more often at a modestly higher reward-given-done (.30 → .58). The arm whose per-task ability actually rose is the one that moved on SWE-bench.

**Takeaway.** On this model, SFT on SWE-smith traces before R2E-Gym RL does not add to what RL from the base reaches in the same 24 updates. The traces teach a finishing style; RL rebuilt the standard SFT's task ability but only to the base + RL level, and on TailSFT it mostly rewarded the finishing style, and neither path ends above 23 / 100. These are one-trial reads, so the 20 vs 23 is a tie; the 13 is a real gap against base + RL (4 / 14 paired).

**Caveat added after a code and weight audit of the two SFT checkpoints (same day).** The TailSFT and standard checkpoints are near-replicates: they sit 5.9e-5 relative L2 apart, against a 3.4e-5 floor between two runs of the unmodified trainer and a 2.7e-4 shift for the SFT itself, and no seed was pinned. So the 13 vs 20 above is not established as a TailSFT effect; the honest reading is that two RL runs from near-identical starts diverged by 7 points on this split after 24 updates, which is the run-to-run spread of the pipeline at one trial, and the same spread applies to the 20 vs 23 comparison with base + RL. The data-side audit found the more likely cause of the SFT regression itself: 39 % of the Kimi training traces are failed trials that still end by declaring the task complete, and the traces are ten times shorter than the base's own working style, so the SFT learned when to stop, not when the fix is right.

**Reproduction.** SFT checkpoints `snowball-kimi_swesmith-sft/full-lr5e-5-ep3` and `full-lr5e-5-ep3-tail25` (export step 96), RL configs `snowball_ttband_{vansft_l454,tailsft_l453}_12n_a` with the band trees named in the gist; policy job directories on JSC Jupiter, happy to attach any trial.

The RST paper trained only on verified successes, self-rolled, at lr 3e-6, so their recipe and ours share little beyond the task generator. spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
## Summary

Multi-host GPU compilation can wait for XLA's hard-coded 24-hour coordination timeout when processes lower different HLO module fingerprints. Iris continues to report every worker as healthy and running, while no optimizer update can occur.

This is broader than #9038. It reproduces with Levanter fused-cross-entropy autotuning disabled and deterministic inferred block sizes, in both the first-class Snowball trainer and the historical Grug trainer used by #8225.

## Reproduction

Launch the 67B Grug SFT train step on eight RNO2A nodes with eight H100s per node and explicit manual mesh axes. Set:

```text
LEVANTER_PALLAS_CE_AUTOTUNE_ON_MISS=0
```

All eight processes load the same native checkpoint and select `batched_xla`. After SPMD partitioning, every process becomes permanently idle. On-demand native thread dumps from every rank show:

```text
xla::CoordinationServiceAgent::GetKeyValue
xla::DistributedRuntimeCoordinationServiceClient::BlockingKeyValueGet
xla::ConfigAssigner::AssignConfigs
xla::gpu::AutotunerPass::RunImpl
xla::gpu::GpuCompiler::OptimizeHloModule
```

The latest reproduction is `/benfeuer/snowball-final-qk157-grug-smoke16-coord/grug-train-hf-smoke`. It remained in this state for more than 20 minutes, versus 264 seconds from W&B creation to the first finite metric in the successful historical #8225 Chat run. W&B system telemetry showed current heartbeats, approximately 66 GB allocated per H100, 0% GPU utilization, and approximately 0.2% host CPU utilization. No update or checkpoint was produced.

## Expected behavior

A distributed compile must either use a common module identity on every process or fail promptly with the mismatched rank fingerprints. It must not wait for keys that no peer can publish under XLA's 24-hour timeout.

## Acceptance criteria

- Multi-host compilation detects rank-divergent HLO module fingerprints before entering distributed autotune assignment.
- Failure is bounded and reports the process index plus each observed fingerprint.
- A regression test supplies divergent per-rank module identities and verifies a prompt diagnostic instead of an unbounded wait.
- Identical-module distributed compilation and single-host compilation are unchanged.

Related to #9038, which covers per-rank Levanter autotuning producing different fused-CE configurations. This issue covers the lower-level XLA wait that still occurs when that autotuning is disabled.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Research: Reproduced on `origin/main` at `054142676a` with two RNO2A hosts (8 H100s each). A matching-module control compiled on both ranks; adding a rank-dependent constant left rank 1 in `CoordinationServiceAgent::GetKeyValue → ConfigAssigner::AssignConfigs → AutotunerPass` while rank 0 compiled. [Control](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fissue-9042-control-20260922) and [divergent probe](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fdlwh%2Fissue-9042-divergent-20260922) contain the task logs. [`initialize_jax`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/054142676a/lib/iris/src/iris/runtime/jax_init.py#L375) joins the ranks, but compilation reaches JAX's backend without a rank identity check.

Proposed Fix: Exchange JAX compile fingerprints across Iris GPU ranks with a bounded timeout before the native backend compile. On mismatch, raise with every observed rank and fingerprint; matching and single-process compiles proceed. Add a regression for divergent and identical rank identities.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body: 🤖 [PR #9364](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9364) adds a bounded JAX compile-key exchange before Iris multi-process GPU compilation. The two-host divergent probe that previously waited in XLA now raises on both ranks with their keys under JAX 0.11.0 and 0.11.1; matching-module controls succeed on both versions. This checks the pre-compile key, so divergence introduced later inside XLA still needs native diagnosis. The 67B train step was not rerun; CI and review are in progress.

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
## Summary

Test **omni-neurons**: a dense-model variant where each layer's **MLP** reads the
concatenation of *every prior sublayer snapshot* instead of just the current
residual stream. Attention is unchanged (it still reads the residual stream).

For layer `n` the MLP input is the concatenation of:
`[embed, {attn_out_i, resid_post_attn_i, mlp_out_i, resid_post_mlp_i for each prior layer i}, attn_out_n, resid_post_attn_n]`
— each `d`-wide, so the MLP input width grows with depth as `d·(4n+3)`. The MLP
still writes a `d`-wide residual delta (asymmetric in/out).

**Research goal:** after training, inspect *where the MLP input neurons point* —
do they attend to the individual layer branch outputs (`attn_out` / `mlp_out`) or
to the accumulated residual-stream sums (`resid_post_attn` / `resid_post_mlp`)?
This is why final checkpoints are saved.

## Exact prompts

> follow agent.md and test an idea called omni-neurons. Lets use the dense model as the baseline. but save the output of every layer, and the sum after its added to the residual stream. The input to layer n will then be a concatenated list of [embed, layer0_attn_out, layer0_resid_post_attn, layer0_mlp_out, layer0_resid_post_mlp, layer1_attn_out, layer1_resid_post_attn...]. So the input dim to layer I scales with the layer. EG layer 6 will have roughly 24x wider dims. First, will this fit at d512?

> oh, lets only use omni input for mlp, not attn.

> yes, run both sizes and raise a github issue. The idea here is we want to investigate after it trains where the input neurons are pointing. To see if they are looking at the layer outputs, or the residual stream sums. So we also need to turn on final checkpoint saving.

## Feasibility (MLP-only omni, d512 dense: d=512, L=6, I=1536, seq=4096, batch=128, 8×H100)

| Item | dense baseline | omni-MLP |
|---|---|---|
| Non-embed params | 18.1M | 131.3M (7.3×) |
| Total params | 34.9M | 148.1M |
| Weights + optimizer state (14 B/param, FSDP /8) | 0.06 GB/gpu | 0.26 GB/gpu |
| Retained snapshot activations (4/layer, bf16, /8) | — | 1.68 GB/gpu |
| **Total-model FLOPs/step** (incl. attn core + embed) | 1× | **~2.9×** |

Fits trivially (single-digit GB/gpu). The binding cost is compute: ~2.9× total
FLOPs → expect ~3× slower wall-clock, so the run must show a real loss gain to
net positive on effective speedup. Params grow ≈ `L²` with depth, so the full
ladder (d1024/d1280) would get much more expensive — a gate-2 consideration.

## Implementation

Branch `fast_track_omni_mlp` @ `95a2cf0a0e` (off the baseline-budget branch).

- `model.py`: `GrugModelConfig.omni_mlp` (dense-only, default off → shared path
  byte-identical). `DenseMLP.init` gains `out_dim` (wide input, `d`-wide output).
  Heterogeneous per-layer MLP widths can't be scanned, so omni blocks are held
  **unrolled** (`Transformer.omni_blocks`) with a Python-loop forward that
  accumulates the snapshot list, per-snapshot RMSNorm (shared width-`d` gain, keeps
  snapshots magnitude-comparable), concatenates, then the wide GatedNorm + MLP.
  Each layer remat'd (`eqx.filter_checkpoint`).
- `optimizer.py`: no change needed — omni's leaves route correctly
  (`w_gate/w_up/w_down` → muonh, `rms_mlp.weight` → adam, `mlp_gated_norm` → muonh).
- `launch.py`: `--omni-mlp` flag (implies `--dense`).

Verified on CPU: per-layer widths = `d·(4i+3)` in / `d` out, non-omni path intact,
optimizer routing correct, concat bookkeeping matches. GPU forward validated by the
launched runs stepping.

## Runs (gate 1: data-matched vs the dense baseline, cw-rno2a, version 2026.09.22)

| run_id | size | steps (data-match) | checkpoints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omni-mlp-d512` | d512 | ~690 | saved (final) |
| `omni-mlp-d768` | d768 | (dense-d768 budget) | saved (final) |

Compare `eval/paloma/macro_loss` and `throughput/tokens_per_second` against the
`fasttrack-baseline` dense d512/d768 runs; gate 1 passes if omni beats the dense
baseline macro loss at **both** scales. Final checkpoints will be analyzed for the
per-snapshot input-weight norms (layer outputs vs residual-stream sums).

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Omni-neuron component ablation** — which snapshots drive the gain, and does it pay off?

Added three component-selection modes to the omni MLP (branch `fast_track_omni_mlp`, commits `fac6c595f3` / `b440292d5b` / `907f97b60e`) and ran the ladder at d512/d768, data-matched, vs the dense baseline. Metric: `eval/paloma/macro_loss`.

| variant (omni MLP input) | d512 | Δ | d768 | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **dense baseline** | 3.6758 | — | 3.2825 | — |
| embed_only (`embed + x_post_attn`, width `2d`) | 3.6325 | −0.043 | 3.2481 | −0.034 |
| outputs-only (`attn_out + mlp_out`; no embed/residual) | 3.6355 | −0.040 | **7.2336** | **diverged** |
| residual-only (`embed + resid_post_attn + resid_post_mlp`) | 3.5819 | −0.094 | 3.1904 | −0.092 |
| outputs + embed (`embed + attn_out + mlp_out`) | 3.5739 | −0.102 | 3.1868 | −0.096 |
| omni-ALL (all four snapshots + embed) | 3.5534 | −0.122 | 3.1735 | −0.109 |

**Findings (consistent across both scales):**
- **omni-ALL is best** (−0.122 / −0.109) but the gain leans on a *combination* of the token identity (`embed`) and the inter-layer history — neither alone does much: `embed_only` −0.03/−0.04, and outputs-without-embed even less.
- **outputs+embed ≈ residual-only** (both ≈ −0.09 to −0.10). Once the MLP has embed + history, sublayer *outputs* and residual-*states* help about equally.
- **outputs-only is not a fair ablation:** it feeds the MLP the attention *delta* (`attn_out`), not the current residual stream (`x_post_attn`) the standard MLP reads. Missing that anchor (and `embed`), it's weakest at d512 and **diverges at d768**. The essential MLP input is the current residual; a fair "output-history" variant would keep `x_post_attn` as the base and add output deltas on top.

**But it is not compute-efficient.** Effective speedup vs dense at d768 (data-matched wall-clock to reach the variant's loss; dense loss-vs-tokens fit `L∞=1.63, α=0.193`):

| variant d768 | loss | tok/s | slower | data-gain | **eff. speedup** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dense | 3.2825 | 2,734,245 | — | — | — |
| omni-ALL | 3.1735 | 506,760 | 5.4× | 1.42× | **0.26** |
| outputs+embed | 3.1868 | 365,071 | 7.5× | 1.36× | **0.18** |

The quality gain is worth only ~1.4× data, nowhere near enough to offset the 5–7× throughput hit from the wide, depth-growing (`d·(4n+3)`) concat MLP → **net ~4–5× slower wall-clock**, and worsening with scale.

**Caveats:** single runs, no seeds (~±0.01–0.02 noise) — the tiers are robust, the small gaps aren't. Throughput here is node/contention-sensitive (outputs+embed measured *slower* than the wider omni-ALL, which is backwards — measurement noise); a back-to-back MFU probe would give clean throughput.

**Verdict:** a real, reproducible quality gain that localizes to *embed + inter-layer history acting together* (with the residual stream as the key MLP input), but not a compute win. The interesting follow-up is the clean matched-factorial (`base = embed + x_post_attn`, add output- vs residual-history on top) to decompose the history contribution without the outputs-only anchoring artifact.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
42% data efficiency gain just from having access to earlier representations is interesting.. There is the direction of attention residuals where you compress these all down into hidden_dim values via some dynamic weighting. The gain after doing that is much smaller. 

Very high dimensional input space makes it easier for the neurons to target the exact input data they want. However we of course pay for this with flops. MoE is about sparsely activating neurons. Is there an inverse where we sparsely query a vast input space? Need better logging of what manifold the activations sit on to get a better sense if querying subset makes any sense.

spillover_issues.author: ClassicLarry
spillover_issues.body:
🤖 **Experiment:** learnable per-layer re-injection of the attention output after the MLP.

**Prompt that initiated this:**
> lets try a new issue where we save the attn output, then after each mlp, we let the residual stream x be x + lambda*attn_output. So the model can learn to upscale, or delete out the info it pulled in from the most recent attn. Make sure the scalars (1 per layer), are plotted on wandb. run it at d512 and d768 on the moe baseline.

**Change** (`experiments/grug/fast_track/model.py`, `Block`): after the MLP residual add, re-inject the block's own attention output scaled by a learnable per-layer scalar:
```
x = x + attn_out           # post-attn residual (unchanged)
...
x = x + mlp_out            # post-mlp residual (unchanged)
x = x + attn_reinject_lambda * attn_out   # NEW: learnable re-injection
```
`attn_reinject_lambda` is one scalar per layer, init **0** (so the model starts identical to the MoE baseline) and routed to the `adam` group. It lets the model amplify (`λ>0`) or subtract out (`λ<0`) the information the most recent attention pulled in, *after* the MLP has read it. Per-layer values are logged to W&B under `attn_reinject/lambda_layer_*`. Flag: `--attn-reinject`. Default off ⇒ field is `None`, no-op, checkpoint-compatible.

**Design:** MoE, d512 and d768, data-matched to the MoE baseline. Metric: `eval/paloma/macro_loss` (baselines d512 3.156 / d768 2.872). Branch `fast-track-attn-reinject`.
